Brush the entrecôtes with mustard, then coat them with the spice mixture and refrigerate for 30 min.
Heat the grill over a high flame, place the entrecôtes on it and cook for 2 to 3 min on each side.
Lower the heat to medium and cook to the desired doneness, turning often, then leave to rest for 10 min.
Slice thinly on the diagonal, against the grain, and serve with potatoes and a green salad.
escalopes-de-poulet-aux-aubergines: Heat the olive oil over a high heat, then fry the finely sliced shallot, the tomatoes cut into wedges and the aubergines cut into cubes.
Cook for 5 minutes over a high heat, stirring, then add the crushed garlic, the lemon cut into wedges, and season with salt and pepper.
Add the curry powder and leave to simmer over a medium heat for 10 minutes.
Cook the chicken escalopes in a frying pan, season with salt and pepper, then arrange them in the serving dish.
Deglaze the pan juices with a little water, spoon them over the escalopes and top with the aubergine preparation.
escalopes-de-veau-au-munster: Brown the veal escalopes for 3 minutes per side in very hot butter, season with salt and pepper, and set aside.
Sweat the finely chopped onion in the cooking juices.
Add the crème fraîche and the rind-free Munster over a low heat.
Let the sauce cook until it is smooth and creamy, then season with salt and pepper.
Spoon the Munster sauce over the escalopes and serve hot with the green salad and wholegrain rice.
escalopes-de-veau-parmesan-amandes: Mix the grated Parmesan and the ground almonds in a bowl.
Beat the egg into an omelette, then season with salt and pepper.
Flour the escalopes on both sides, dip them in the egg, then coat them in the Parmesan and almond mixture.
Heat the butter and oil in a non-stick frying pan, then brown the escalopes over a medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side.
estomac-de-porc-farci-a-la-viande-et-aux: Stuffed Pig's Stomach with Meat and Vegetables (Saumagen)
Soak the pig's stomach overnight, then close it with string across two openings.
Cut the meat and potatoes into small cubes.
Sauté the onion, carrot and parsley in butter, then crush the garlic.
Mix everything with the bread soaked in milk and eggs, season generously with salt, pepper, marjoram and nutmeg, then stuff the stomach and close the third opening.
Place the stomach in hot water without letting it boil and cook for 2 to 3 hours, then slice into 2 cm pieces and serve with mashed potatoes and sauerkraut.
fajitas-au-poulet: Cut the chicken into pieces of about 2.5 cm, then season them with turmeric, salt and black pepper.
Heat the olive oil over a high heat in a large frying pan, add the chicken with the cumin and chilli flakes, then cook.
Slice the peppers and onion into strips while the meat is cooking.
When the chicken is well cooked, add the vegetables and stir often until they are tender, then remove from the heat.
Serve in tortillas with cheese, crème fraîche, lettuce and tomato.
faten-wake-bouillie-de-haricots-haoussa: Rinse the dried beans, then cook them for 40 to 60 minutes over a medium heat in water until they are tender and the water is almost absorbed.
Add the sliced onion, chopped tomato and groundnut oil to the cooked beans, then simmer for 10 to 15 minutes until thickened.
Season with salt, then cook for a further 5 to 10 minutes, stirring, until a well-bound porridge is obtained.
filet-mignon-grille-reduction-au-cognac: Season the filet mignons on both sides with salt, then coat them with mustard and press them into the cracked black pepper.
Grill the filets for 1 minute per side over high heat, then finish over medium heat until they reach 60 °C at the centre, and keep warm.
Boil the cognac over high heat in a small saucepan until reduced by a third.
Serve the filets topped with the cognac reduction, with brown rice and a tomato salad.
fleischschnacka: Beat the egg into an omelette, season with salt, then gradually add the flour until you obtain a supple dough, and leave it to rest.
Finely chop the cooked meat with the onion and parsley, mix with the egg, season with salt and pepper.
Roll out the dough into a 3 mm rectangle, spread the filling over it leaving 1 to 2 cm free at the edges, roll up and seal the edge with a little water, then cut into slices of 2 to 3 cm.
Brown the slices in very hot oil, place them in a dish, cover with stock and white wine, then bake for 20 to 30 min at 180 °C, turning them halfway through cooking.
fletan-en-tempura-au-four-aioli-a-la-cor: Beat the egg in a bowl, add the iced water, then the flour and mix without overworking the batter.
Lightly oil an ovenproof dish, dip the halibut pieces in the batter and place them in the dish.
Bake for 20 min at 180 °C until the fish is lightly golden.
Mix the mayonnaise, olive oil, garlic, coriander, lemon juice and pepper to make the aioli.
Serve the halibut with the aioli.
fondue-normande: Trim the rinds from the cheeses and cut them into cubes.
Rub the fondue pot with the crushed shallot, place the cheese cubes in it and add the calvados.
Dilute the cornflour in the milk, pour into the pot and heat gently while stirring, then add the cream, season with salt and pepper and grate in nutmeg.
Bring to the boil, stirring constantly until the mixture is smooth, then serve with the bread cubes.
frijoles-antioquenos-ragout-de-haricots-: Antioquian beans, Colombian red bean stew
Fry the spring onion in the oil until it starts to turn golden.
Add the tomato, cumin, allspice and vegetable stock, then stir to combine.
Add the cooked red beans, the plantain and the water, then bring to the boil.
Cover and cook for 30 min over a medium heat, then add a little water if needed and season with salt and pepper.
frittata-aux-asperges: Beat the eggs with the milk, basil, salt and pepper in a bowl.
Preheat the oven to 175 °C and heat the olive oil in an ovenproof frying pan over a medium heat.
Fry the garlic for 1 min, then add the asparagus and leave to soften for 5 min.
Pour the eggs into the pan, cook for 4 min, scatter over the parmesan, then put in the oven for 3 min until the top puffs up and turns golden.
Cut the frittata into portions and serve with wholemeal bread and a tomato salad.
galette-de-pommes-de-terre: Peel and grate the potatoes, then rinse them in cold water to remove the starch.
Drain and squeeze the potatoes well, then finely chop the onion.
Mix the eggs, milk, flour, salt, pepper and nutmeg, then add the onion and potatoes.
Fry small, tightly packed portions in a very hot, oiled frying pan, cooking both sides.
galettes-de-tofu: Blend the tofu, garlic, onion, parsley and flour until you have a supple dough.
Add the oat flakes, finely sliced shallot, tamari, lemon mustard and sesame, then mix thoroughly.
Shape into small round patties about 1 cm thick.
Heat the groundnut oil in a frying pan and brown the patties over a high heat, 5 minutes on each side.
garbure: Soak the white beans in water for at least 24 hours the day before.
Bring the shredded cabbage, beans and duck confit to the boil in salted water, then skim.
Reduce the heat, cover and cook for 2 to 3 hours.
Add the carrots, leek, crushed garlic, pepper and potatoes, then simmer gently for a good hour.
Adjust the seasoning with a little salt and serve hot with a piece of duck per person.
gaspacho-manchois-aux-fruits-de-mer: Clean the mussels, shell the prawns, and cut the monkfish and red pepper into small pieces.
Sauté everything with the garlic and tomato in the oil.
Add the buckwheat galette cut into pieces and the necessary water.
At the start of cooking, add one clove of garlic and the parsley crushed in a mortar.
Leave to rest for 10 minutes before serving.
gboma-dessi-ragout-d-epinards-togolais-a: Gboma dessi, Togolese spinach stew with meiwa
Fry the finely chopped onion and garlic with the ginger in palm oil for 2 minutes.
Add the meat, the chilli, a stock cube, salt and enough water to cover, then cook in a casserole for about 40 minutes.
Cook the spinach shoots in salted water for 15 minutes, drain and finely chop.
Sprinkle the meat with aniseed, ajwain, cardamom and ginger, then stir in the tomato purée and leave to simmer for 25 minutes with the reserved stock.
Add the spinach and then the meat, leave to simmer for 15 minutes and serve with akoumé.
ghormeh-sabzi-ragout-iranien-aux-herbes: Cook the white beans for 1 hour in simmering water, then drain.
Fry the sliced onion in rapeseed oil over high heat for 1 to 2 minutes, add the minced beef and cook for 1 to 2 minutes.
Lower the heat to minimum, add the parsley, spinach, coriander and ghormeh sabzi herbs, then pour in 0.5 L of boiling water.
Add the beans and simmer gently for 30 minutes, then stir in the pierced limes, turmeric, salt and pepper, and continue for 20 minutes.
Steam the rice and serve it with the hot stew, the rice being flavoured with saffron.
githeri: Rinse the maize and beans, then soak them overnight in water.
Drain, place in a large pan covered with water and cook until tender, about 1 hour.
Fry the finely sliced onion in the vegetable oil until golden, then add the tomato and cook for a few minutes.
Stir in the cooked maize and beans, season with salt and simmer for 10 minutes, adding a little water if needed.
goulash: Cut the meat, onion and garlic into small pieces, then brown the onion in the oil in a casserole dish.
Add the meat and garlic, brown, then add the paprika without letting it burn, water, cumin, pepper and salt.
Add the diced tomato and pepper, then leave to simmer for a long time.
Stir in the carrots, celery and swede partway through cooking, then add the potatoes once the meat is tender.
Serve hot, sprinkled with chopped parsley.
gratin-de-pates-et-viande-hachee: Cook the pasta, drain it and cool it under cold running water.
Finely slice the onion, dice the bacon and fry both in a little oil, then add the minced meat, followed by the parsley and rosemary.
Butter a dish, spread half the pasta in it, cover with the meat, then add slices of tomato and finish with the remaining pasta.
Mix the milk, egg, salt and pepper, pour this mixture over the bake, then sprinkle with grated cheese.
gyuvetch-ragout-bulgare-au-b-uf: Brown the minced beef in the oil, cover with water, cook until tender, then season with soy sauce.
Sprinkle the aubergine with salt, leave to rest, pat dry, then cut each slice into quarters.
Sauté the carrot, aubergine, potato and okra in the oil, add the tomato and onion with a little water, cook until the vegetables are just tender, then add the red pepper and turn off the heat.
Combine the meat with the cooking juices and the vegetables, pour into a clay pot, top with chilli, cover and bake for 20 minutes at 200 °C.
Sprinkle with chopped parsley and serve.
gateau-au-fromage-a-la-mode-d-obwald: Line the quiche dish with the shortcrust pastry and prick the base with a fork.
Cover the pastry with the sbrinz and half of the grated emmental.
In a bowl, mix the flour, egg yolk, milk, cream, nutmeg, salt and pepper, then pour over the cheese.
Bake in a medium oven for 30 min, until the top is golden and the filling is set, then serve warm with a green salad.
haggis: Poach the beef heart for 1 hour 10 minutes in a covered pot of cold water, then add the liver and lamb and cook for 20 minutes.
Drain, leave to cool, reserve 1 cup of the stock, then roughly chop the meats.
Mix the meats, toasted oatmeal, onion, whisky, egg nog and spices, then divide into three portions.
Stuff the casings soaked in vinegar and salt, tie off the ends, prick and steam for 1 hour 20 minutes.
Serve in slices with a sauce made from the reserved stock.
haleem-hyderabadi-au-ble-et-a-la-viande: Haleem Hyderabadi with wheat and mutton
Remove the bran from the wheat, rinse it, then soak it for 2 hours.
Blend the ginger, garlic, chilli and salt into a paste, rub it over the mutton and leave to marinate for 1 hour.
Pressure-cook the wheat and meat for about 45 minutes, then chop finely and reduce to a fine purée.
Heat the oil, fry the sliced onions until golden, then add the turmeric and garam masala.
Add the purée and cook over a gentle heat, stirring, until the mixture pulls away from the sides of the pan, then adjust the seasoning and serve hot with lime wedges, coriander and fried onions.
hamburger-stoup: Fry the finely sliced onion in a splash of oil until translucent.
Add the minced beef and break it up until well browned.
In a large casserole, combine the meat, tomatoes, sweetcorn, peas, celery, potatoes, stocks, rice, salt and pepper, then cover with water.
Cover and bake at 160 °C (325 °F) for 6 hours, then serve.
haricots-noirs-sud-ouest-et-riz: Heat the drained black beans with the diced tomato and cumin in a saucepan over a medium heat for 8 min.
Cook the rice in unsalted simmering water, then drain.
Serve the beans on the hot rice with sliced tomatoes in a salad.
hobo-burgers: Mix the Worcestershire sauce into the minced beef, then shape into 2 patties.
Place each patty on a cabbage leaf laid over a sheet of aluminium foil.
Top with slices of onion and potato, add a knob of butter, then season with salt and pepper.
Cover with a second cabbage leaf, seal the parcels and cook for 20 to 30 minutes over medium embers, turning twice.
Serve the parcels open, with a green salad.
homard-thermidor: Mix the egg yolks with the double cream in a bowl and set aside.
Melt the butter over a low heat in a large saucepan.
Add the lobster and the sherry, then sauté over a medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed.
Gradually pour in the cream and egg mixture, stirring constantly, and remove from the heat as soon as the sauce thickens.
Fill the lobster shell with the filling, sprinkle with gruyère, salt and pepper, then grill for 3 to 8 minutes until golden. Serve with brown rice and green salad.
hooman-de-crevettes-curry-goan: Put the prawns, onion, chicken drumstick and asafoetida in a saucepan with a little water, and cook until the prawns and chicken are cooked through.
Blend the grated coconut, chillies, turmeric, black pepper and tamarind into a smooth paste, adding very little water.
Add the paste to the prawns, bring to the boil, then season with salt to taste.
Serve piping hot with brown rice and a green salad.
hotpot-de-lancashire: Cut the lamb into cubes and preheat the oven to 170 °C (gas mark 3).
Arrange a layer of potatoes at the bottom of an ovenproof dish, cover with chopped onion, then add a layer of lamb sprinkled with herbs.
Repeat the layers until the dish is full, finishing with a layer of potatoes.
Pour in boiling water to cover, then bake for at least 1 hour.
Serve piping hot with green vegetables or a salad.
jambalaya-a-la-dinde: Mix the salt, savory, basil, thyme and cumin, then grind to a powder.
Chop the tomatoes into pieces, reserving their juice.
Lightly sweat the celery in the butter without letting it colour.
Add the tomatoes, rice, stock, turkey and the spices, then bring to the boil.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes, then remove the bay leaf before serving.
jollof-de-riz-et-haricots-blancs-nigeria: Nigerian jollof rice and white beans
Rinse the white beans, then boil them in water until tender and drain.
Blend the chilli, tomatoes and onion to a purée.
Heat a thin layer of oil, add the purée, season with the stock and salt, then simmer for 3 min.
Stir in the rice and beans, cook for 5 min, then serve.
kanda-ragout-de-poulet-a-la-cacahuete: Toast the peanuts in the oven for a few minutes, then rub them to remove the skins and grind them to a fine powder in a blender.
Heat the rapeseed oil in a large casserole dish over a medium heat, fry the chopped onion until translucent, then add the chicken and brown it.
Add the garlic, tomato and pepper, and cook for a few minutes until they soften.
Stir in the tomato purée, peanut butter, peanut powder, paprika, thyme, salt and pepper, then pour in the stock and bring to the boil.
Reduce the heat, cover and leave to simmer for 1 to 1½ hours until the meat is tender, adjust the seasoning and serve hot with brown rice.
karahi-de-poulet-au-poivron-et-a-la-toma: Chicken karahi with red pepper and tomato
Fry the red peppers in rapeseed oil in a wok or sauté pan until golden.
Add the chicken marinated in garlic paste and salt, and cook over a low heat until it becomes slightly tender.
Stir in the diced tomatoes and cook over a low heat for 15 min, stirring.
Garnish with sliced chilli and coriander, then serve.
katogo-melange-ougandais-de-bananes-vert: Katogo, Ugandan green banana and bean mix
Peel and cut the green bananas into pieces, then set aside.
Fry the finely sliced onion in the vegetable oil until lightly golden.
Add the green pepper and grated tomato, season with salt, then cook for 1 minute, stirring.
Add the bananas, stir for 1 minute, pour in the water and cook for 10 minutes over a medium heat.
Stir in the cumin, curry powder and pepper, then add the rinsed and drained white beans and leave to simmer for 12 minutes.
kedjenou-de-poulet-aux-legumes: Season the chicken with salt, pepper, ginger paste, garlic, thyme, smoked paprika and stock, then leave to marinate in the fridge for 2 hours.
Arrange the tomatoes, onion, spring onion, red pepper and aubergine in a casserole dish, then add the chicken and the bay leaf.
Cover the casserole dish and bake for 1 hour at 175 °C, shaking the dish once or twice without opening it.
Serve the kedjenou piping hot with slices of wholemeal bread.
khara-pongal-bouillie-de-riz-et-haricots: Khara pongal, rice and mung bean porridge
Cook the rice and mung beans with the turmeric in the water for 20 minutes until soft and tender.
Fry the cashew nuts in a little ghee until golden, then remove them.
Heat the remaining ghee and the rapeseed oil, then fry the mustard seeds, cumin, green chilli and curry leaves.
Add the rice and mung beans, warm through, add a little water if needed, season with salt and pepper, then scatter over the cashew nuts.
khichuri-bengali-au-riz-et-lentilles: Khichuri Bengali with rice and lentils
Rinse the rice and lentils separately under cold water, then soak the lentils for 30 minutes.
Drain the lentils and dry-roast them in a pan for a few minutes until fragrant.
Heat the butter in a casserole dish, add the bay leaf, crushed spices, ginger and cumin, then fry for 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the chilli, rice, lentils, salt and turmeric, stir for 3 minutes, pour in the hot water, cover and simmer over low heat for 10 minutes.
Fry the sliced onion in the remaining butter, spoon it over the khichuri and sprinkle with coriander. Serve with a tomato salad.
khinkali: Finely mince the beef, pork and onions, then season with black pepper, salt and half a glass of hot water.
Sift the flour, add salt, slowly pour in the water and knead until you have a firm dough.
Roll the dough very thin, cut out rounds and fill each with a spoonful of the filling, then pinch closed and twist the edges.
Drop the khinkali into boiling salted water, stir gently, then cook for a further 6 to 7 minutes once they rise to the surface. Drain with a slotted spoon and serve hot.
kofta-d-agneau: Mix the minced lamb, paprika, cumin, cinnamon, cayenne pepper, parsley, coriander and mint until well combined.
Shape the mixture into small elongated sausages about 5 to 8 cm long.
Grill the kofta for about 4 minutes on each side, turning halfway through cooking, until lightly coloured.
Leave to rest for a few moments and serve with potatoes and a green salad.
kofta-egyptiennes: Mix the minced beef, finely sliced onion, garlic, parsley, coriander, cumin, paprika, salt and pepper until well combined.
Shape the mixture into elongated meatballs of uniform size.
Heat the olive oil over a medium heat in a frying pan or griddle pan.
Cook the kofta for 10 to 12 minutes, turning them regularly, until well browned and cooked through.
Serve hot with a tomato salad and brown rice.
koshari: Cook the basmati rice, green lentils and chickpeas until tender, then cook the macaroni al dente and drain everything.
Layer the rice, lentils, macaroni and then the chickpeas in a dish to form the base.
Fry the sliced onion in olive oil until crispy, then set aside a portion for the garnish.
Dilute the tomato purée in the water, add the cumin, pepper and vinegar, reduce over a high heat then simmer over a low heat.
Top the base with the tomato sauce and crispy onions, season to taste and serve with a green salad and tomatoes.
kuku-paka-poulet-au-lait-de-coco: Mix the chicken with the lemon juice, garlic, ginger, curry powder, turmeric, salt, pepper and oil, then leave to marinate for 30 min.
Grill or roast the chicken in the oven until lightly charred and partially cooked.
Fry the onion in the oil over a medium heat until soft.
Add the garlic, ginger, chilli, tomato, tomato purée, curry powder, cumin and coriander, then cook until the tomato breaks down.
Pour in the coconut milk, add the chicken and simmer for 20 to 30 min. Serve with brown rice and fresh coriander.
lasagnes-au-tofu: Heat the olive oil, fry the onion and garlic, then add the mushrooms and cook for 2 minutes, stirring.
Pour in the tomato sauce, add the bay leaf and oregano, leave to simmer until thickened, then remove from the heat and stir in half of the parsley.
Mix the chopped spinach, crumbled tofu and the remaining parsley in a large bowl.
Assemble the lasagne by alternating tomato sauce, pasta and the spinach-tofu mixture, finishing with the vegan béchamel.
Bake at 175 °C for about 50 minutes until golden, then leave to rest for 15 minutes before serving.
lieu-jaune-en-papillote-de-cresson: Preheat the oven to 225 °C and cut two squares of baking paper, each about 45 cm.
Wash the watercress, spin it dry, remove the thick stalks, then spread a first layer of it in each parcel along with the chopped onion.
Season the pieces of pollock lightly with pepper, place them on the watercress, then add a second layer of watercress and the potato slices.
Seal the parcels tightly and set them in a Pyrex dish.
Bake for 45 minutes at 225 °C until the pollock is cooked through, then serve.
linguine-au-pesto-d-epinards: Lightly sauté the garlic in a pan, without cooking it through completely.
Chop the garlic in a food processor, gradually add the spinach, then the olive oil and blend. Set aside in a bowl.
Heat the chicken breast over a medium heat on a grill or in a pan, then cook for about 10 minutes, turning it over.
Cook the linguine in boiling salted water, then drain. Warm the mangetout over a low heat for 5 minutes with a little olive oil.
Reheat the pasta with the pesto over a low heat, plate up, and top with feta, olives, mangetout and slices of chicken. Serve.
locrio-riz-au-poulet-dominicain: Heat the rapeseed oil in a casserole over a high heat, add the sugar and let it caramelise to a light brown without burning.
Brown the chicken pieces on all sides, then set them aside.
Fry the onion, garlic and stock in the casserole, then add the rice, the chicken, the tomato purée, the thyme, the salt, the pepper and the olives.
Bring to the boil over a high heat, stirring until the liquid is absorbed, cover, reduce the heat and cook for 15 min.
Drizzle with oil, stir, cook for a further 10 min while stirring, then serve.
maffe-ragout-de-b-uf-a-la-cacahuete: Brown the minced beef in hot vegetable oil, then set aside.
Sauté the finely chopped onion and garlic, add the peanut butter and let it melt over a low heat.
Add the cumin, paprika, chilli, salt and pepper, then pour in the vegetable stock, stirring to obtain a smooth sauce.
Return the meat, cover and simmer for 30 minutes, then add the carrot, potato, pepper, okra and spinach for 15 to 20 minutes.
Serve hot with the chopped coriander.
maffe-ragout-de-b-uf-a-la-cacahuete-2: Boil the minced meat with the onion and a pinch of salt in a pan of water for 10 minutes, then drain.
Fry the meat in a pan with a drizzle of oil until golden.
Blend the tomato purée with the black pepper and a little water until you have a smooth mixture.
Pour the blended mixture into a pan, add the peanut butter and the meat, then stir until thickened. Serve with brown rice and steamed green beans.
mafrum-bil-lahm-pommes-de-terre-farcies-: Boil the sliced potatoes in salted water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Fry the finely chopped onion and garlic in olive oil until translucent.
Add the minced beef and brown it, then season with cumin, paprika, cayenne pepper, salt and pepper.
Stuff the flattened potato slices with the meat, arrange them in a dish and spoon over the chopped tomatoes.
Cover with foil and bake for 45 minutes at 180 °C, then for 10 to 15 minutes uncovered. Sprinkle with parsley before serving.
magret-de-canard-a-la-nipponne: Mix the soy sauce, sweet wine, ginger and crushed garlic to make the marinade.
Remove the skin from the duck breasts, keep one piece aside, cut the meat into large cubes and marinate them for 15 minutes.
Render the duck skin over a high heat for a few minutes.
Remove the skin, sear the marinated duck cubes over a high heat for 3 to 4 minutes, then set them aside in the serving dish.
Heat the remaining marinade with 6 cl of water, strain it, spoon it over the duck cubes, sprinkle with chives and serve hot.
maquereau-marine: Clean and scale the mackerel, then arrange it in an ovenproof dish.
Mix the bay leaf, mace, thyme and onion, season with salt, then pour over the fish.
Bake in a medium oven for 45 minutes.
Arrange the fish carefully, spoon over its strained juices, let it cool slightly and serve with wholemeal rice and green salad.
maraq-ragout-de-poulet-aux-epices: Fry the finely chopped onion in the vegetable oil for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and tomato and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the chicken and the spices (cumin, ground coriander, turmeric), season with salt and brown for 5 minutes.
Pour in 1 litre of water, bring to the boil, then leave to simmer for 25 minutes.
Add the carrot, potato and courgette and cook for a further 20 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Scatter over fresh coriander and serve piping hot.
menemen-aux-ufs-oignon-poivron-et-tomate: Menemen with eggs, onion, pepper and tomato
Blanch, peel, deseed and dice the tomatoes.
Fry the sliced onion and red pepper in olive oil until soft.
Add the oregano and paprika if using, then the tomatoes, and cook for 5 min.
Stir in the parsley, season with salt and pepper, then pour in the beaten eggs and stir until cooked.
mesir-wat-ragout-de-lentilles-epicees-et: Mesir wat, Ethiopian spiced lentil stew
Rinse the lentils, then cook them for 15 to 20 minutes in unsalted simmering water, and set aside.
Fry the chopped onion in the olive oil for 5 minutes, add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the berbere, the tomato purée, the cumin, the turmeric, salt and pepper, then add the lentils along with their cooking water.
Leave to simmer for 20 minutes over a low heat, stirring, and adjust the seasoning.
Sprinkle with chopped parsley and serve hot.
mini-burgers-grilles: Preheat the oven to 120 °C and a grill to 175 °C.
Toast the buns in the warm oven, then set aside.
Mix the salt, pepper, garlic powder and rosemary.
Shape the meat into patties, brush with olive oil, season on both sides and grill for 2 to 3 min per side.
Spread the buns with mayonnaise, top with the patties and serve warm.
miyan-giyada-soupe-nigeriane-aux-cacahue: Cook the meat with the onion, salt and stock until tender, then keep the stock.
Blend the peanuts until you have a smooth paste.
Add the peanut paste and the chilli to the stock, stirring so it does not catch.
Stir in the palm oil, then the spinach, and let it thicken until the oil rises to the surface.
Adjust the seasoning and serve the soup with the meat.
miyan-taushe-soupe-haoussa-au-potiron: Cook the minced meat with the onion, stock cubes and water until tender.
Add the pumpkin in pieces and cook for 10 to 15 minutes, then mash some of the pumpkin to thicken the soup.
Stir in the fermented locust bean seeds and the palm oil, mix well and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add a little water if needed to reach the desired consistency, and serve with semolina or rice.
mofongo-puree-de-plantains-au-porc-crous: Peel the plantains and cut them into 2.5 cm diagonal pieces.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan, fry the plantains for 3 min 30 sec on each side, then flatten them with a plate.
Return the plantains to the hot oil and fry for 1 min on each side, then drain on kitchen paper.
Mash the still-warm plantains with the garlic, fat, stock, pork, salt and pepper.
Serve with green salad and tomato salad.
moules-mariniere: Fry the finely chopped shallot and the garlic clove in the butter until golden.
Add the sherry and the bay leaf to a large frying pan.
Add the fried shallot, the mussels, salt and plenty of pepper, then cook over medium-high heat, shaking the pan, for 6 to 8 minutes.
Remove the mussels as soon as their shells open, and discard any that remain closed.
Serve the mussels in warm bowls, sprinkled with parsley.
moussaka: Salt the aubergine slices on both sides, leave to degorge for 1 hour, rinse, drain and pat dry.
Fry the chopped onion in olive oil until translucent, then add the minced lamb and cook for 10 minutes, crumbling it as it cooks.
Add the white wine, tomato pulp, parsley, cinnamon and pepper, cover and simmer for 15 minutes, then uncover and continue for 10 minutes.
Make the béchamel: melt the butter, add the flour and cook for 2 minutes, gradually pour in the milk, then stir in the beaten egg and parmesan, and season with salt and pepper.
Sear the aubergines, layer the aubergines and the filling alternately in a dish, cover with the béchamel and gratin for 45 minutes in an oven preheated to 210 °C.
muchomo-de-b-uf-ougandais: Mix the oil, lemon juice, cumin, garlic powder, cardamom, cayenne pepper and salt together in a mixing bowl.
Add the minced beef and chopped onion, mix well and leave to marinate in the fridge for 9 to 10 hours, or overnight.
Preheat the grill to high and the oven to 90°C.
Thread the meat and pieces of onion alternately onto metal skewers.
Grill the skewers for about 2 minutes on each side until a crust forms, then finish in the oven for 45 minutes at 90°C and serve with peri peri sauce for dipping.
navarin-d-agneau: Fry the thinly sliced onions in the butter, add the lamb pieces and brown them with the flour.
Add the tomato purée, cover with water, season with salt and pepper, add the bouquet garni and cook for 30 minutes with the lid on.
Add the carrots, turnips and peas, cover and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the potatoes, cover and cook for a further 30 minutes, then serve hot.
nilagang-baka-bouilli-de-b-uf-aux-legume: Nilagang baka, beef and vegetable boil
Boil the chopped beef with the black pepper, onion, corn and potato in salted water for 40 min.
Add the green cabbage cut into wedges and cook for a further 10 min.
Add the chives cut into 7 cm lengths and simmer for 2 min.
Serve the broth with the vegetables and meat in a large bowl.
nyama-yemombe-ragout-de-b-uf-zimbabween: Heat the oil over a medium heat, then fry the onion and garlic for 1 min.
Add the minced beef and brown it for 10 min.
Stir in the tomato, paprika and curry powder, then simmer for 20 min over a low heat with the stock.
Add the green pepper 5 min before the end, then season with salt and pepper.
Scatter over the coriander and serve with brown rice.
pabellon-criollo-b-uf-hache-a-la-sauce-t: Pabellón criollo, minced beef in tomato and cumin sauce
Fry the finely chopped onion and garlic in the olive oil for 5 minutes over a medium heat.
Add the tomatoes, cumin and salt, then simmer over a low heat for 30 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce is thick.
Cook the minced beef in the sauce, breaking it up, until it is well cooked through.
Serve with brown rice and green beans.
paella: Cut the chicken and rabbit into small cubes and season them generously with salt.
Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a paella pan, brown the meat for 5 minutes, then add the chopped tomato.
Add the vegetables, lower the heat and sprinkle over the paprika.
Pour in the water, bring to the boil, add the mussels and the saffron, and cook for a few minutes.
Add the rice, lower the heat and cook until the liquid is absorbed, then serve with wholemeal rice and a tomato salad.
paella-roja: Boil the mussels in water for 2 minutes, remove any that have opened, then simmer the shells, onion, pepper, garlic and bay leaf for 30 minutes to make a stock.
Heat the olive oil, brown the salted chicken, add the garlic, then the tomatoes, paprika, onion and pepper to make a sofrito.
Add the coloured stock, bring to the boil, then pour in the rice and cook over a medium heat for 30 to 40 minutes, stirring little.
Add the crab, squid and scallops without stirring, cover for 10 minutes, then place the mussels on top and serve.
paella-valencienne: Brown the pieces of chicken, rabbit and duck in hot olive oil until golden.
Add the diced peppers and garlic, then the tomatoes, paprika and rice, and mix well.
Pour in the saffron stock to cover, add the rosemary and white beans, then simmer over a low heat for 10 minutes.
Cook without stirring for about 15 minutes until the rice is tender and a golden crust forms on the bottom.
Arrange the pepper strips in a circle and serve.
paella-vegetalienne: Cook the rice for 25 minutes in salted water.
Place the tomatoes, onions, garlic, beans, carrots, peas, pepper, mushrooms, rice and saffron in the casserole.
Cook over a low heat for 2 hours 30 minutes, then add the pitted olives 30 minutes before the end.
At the time of serving, add the olive oil, chopped parsley and season with salt.
pain-de-viande-aux-pois-chiches: Drain the chickpeas, reserving the liquid, then mash them into a purée.
Mix the purée, the liquid, the meat, the milk, the salt, the pepper, the Worcestershire sauce, the garlic powder, the sage, the mustard and the oat flakes.
Pour the mixture into an ungreased loaf tin, spread the ketchup on top, then bake for 1 h to 1 h 15.
Leave to rest for 15 minutes before slicing, and serve with the green salad and tomatoes.
palette-aux-lentilles-et-aux-saucisses: Pickled pork shoulder with lentils and sausages
Soak the lentils for 4 to 5 hours in cold water, then drain.
Cook the pork shoulder for 45 to 60 minutes in boiling water, removing half the water after 30 minutes and replacing it with fresh water.
Remove the pork shoulder, add the lentils, carrot, leek, onion and garlic, then simmer for 30 to 45 minutes.
Return the meat to the pan 5 minutes before serving, slice and arrange on top of the lentils.
paneer-butter-masala: Fry the paneer in the ghee, then set aside.
Fry the onion with the garlic and ginger paste until golden brown.
Add the diced pepper and tomato, then the spices, lemon juice and Greek yoghurt, and cook over a medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add the paneer and leave to simmer over a low heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Serve with brown rice and a tomato salad.
parmigiana-de-poulet: Heat the rapeseed oil in a thick-based frying pan over a medium heat.
Flatten the chicken breast to about 1 cm thick, season with salt, pepper and garlic powder.
Dust the chicken in flour, shake off the excess, then fry for 3 minutes on each side until golden.
Warm the tomato purée with the stock, oregano and basil until simmering, then spoon the sauce over the chicken.
Scatter over the mozzarella and parmesan, pop under the grill for 30 to 60 seconds while watching closely, then serve with a green salad and tomatoes.
paupiettes-de-chou-farcies-a-la-sauce-to: Stuffed cabbage parcels in tomato sauce
Preheat the oven to 175 °C and drop the cabbage leaves into boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain.
Mix the minced beef, milk, egg, cooked rice, onion, salt and pepper, then divide into 12 portions.
Place one portion of stuffing on each leaf, roll up and secure with a cocktail stick.
Arrange the rolls in an ovenproof dish, coat with tomato purée, tomatoes, sugar, water and vinegar, cover and bake for 40 minutes.
Remove the rolls, take out the cocktail sticks, thicken the sauce with the cornflour dissolved in cold water, then serve.
paupiettes-de-chou-vert-a-la-dinde-et-a-: Turkey and barley stuffed cabbage rolls
Cook the pearl barley for 30 minutes in the vegetable stock, then drain and leave to cool.
Blanch the whole cabbage for 5 minutes in boiling water, then separate 10 to 12 large leaves.
Mix the barley, turkey, onion, garlic, dill and salt, then fill each leaf and roll up tightly.
Arrange the cabbage rolls in a dish over the tomato, paprika and vinegar sauce, cover and bake for 1 hour at 175 °C.
picadillo-au-b-uf-pommes-de-terre-et-tom: Picadillo with beef, potatoes and tomatoes
Heat the rapeseed oil over medium-high heat, then add the onion, garlic, red pepper and spices.
When the pepper starts to colour, add the minced beef and brown for 7 minutes, breaking it up well.
Add the diced potatoes, the vegetable stock and the chopped tomatoes.
Simmer over a low heat, stirring from time to time, until the picadillo thickens.
Serve hot with wholegrain rice and a side salad of tomatoes.
picadillo-cubain: Brown the minced beef in half of the olive oil over a high heat, then drain and set aside.
Fry the green pepper in the remaining oil until lightly golden.
Add the tomato sauce, cumin and oregano, bring to the boil, then leave to simmer for 20 min, stirring from time to time.
Stir in the beef, raisins, black olives and vinegar, season with salt and pepper, then boil for 10 min.
Serve the picadillo with brown rice and green beans.
pilaf-est-africain-au-b-uf: Cook the minced beef for 15 min in water with the ginger and garlic paste, the grated tomato and onion, then set the stock aside.
Heat the vegetable oil and fry the cumin, cardamom, pepper, cinnamon and clove until they start to crackle.
Add the sliced onion, the turmeric, the ground coriander and the garlic paste, then stir in the cooked meat and mix for 2 min.
Pour in the stock and the rice, season with salt, cook over high heat for 3 min, then cover and leave to cook over low heat until the water is absorbed, before resting off the heat for 5 min.
pilau-de-riz-traditionnel: Rinse the rice several times and leave it to soak while you prepare the rest.
Fry the finely sliced onion in the oil over a low heat, then add the crushed garlic, spices and salt.
Add the tomato, then the minced meat and brown it well, then stir in the drained rice and the chickpeas.
Pour in 575 ml of hot water, bring to the boil, cover and cook for 25 minutes over a very low heat.
Leave to rest off the heat for 5 minutes, then serve with a tomato salad and green salad.
pilons-de-poulet-rotis-aux-epices: Mix the paprika, onion powder, chilli powder and salt in a bowl.
Pat the chicken drumsticks dry with kitchen paper, then coat them in olive oil and the spice mixture.
Arrange the drumsticks in a baking dish and roast for 25 minutes until the skin is golden and crisp.
Serve hot with brown rice and green salad.
pizza-au-thon: Spread the dough out in a dish and top it with crushed tomatoes.
Flake the drained tuna over the pizza and sprinkle with grated comté.
Bake in the oven for 20 min at 200 °C.
pizza-aux-moules: Clean and scrape the mussels, then rinse them well under plenty of cold water.
Cook the mussels for 5 minutes with the finely chopped shallot, chopped parsley, white wine and curry powder, then remove the meat from the shells.
Reduce the cooking juices with the cream to obtain a thick sauce, adding a little cornflour if needed, then stir the mussels into it.
Spread the dough in a pie dish, spoon over the sauce and scatter the diced mozzarella.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes in a hot oven at 220 °C, then serve with a green salad.
pizza-yakiniku-au-b-uf: Knead the flour, yeast, sugar, water and salt, then leave the dough to rest for 10 minutes.
Fry the onion and red pepper in the oil for 10 seconds in a non-stick pan.
Add the minced beef, mirin, soy sauce, oyster sauce and diluted cornflour, then cook until thickened.
Roll out the dough to 10 cm in diameter, top with tomato sauce and the meat, then bake for 20 minutes at 220 °C.
Serve hot with the remaining sauce and tomatoes on the side as a salad.
poisson-blanc-aigre-doux-en-cocotte: Sweet and sour white fish casserole
Mix the lemon juice, tomato purée, sugar and turmeric until you have a smooth sauce.
Fry the sliced onion in the hot oil until golden, then spread it in an ovenproof dish.
Fry the peppers and chilli for 2 minutes, place them over the onion, then cover with half the tomatoes, the garlic, salt and pepper.
Sear the fish for 1 minute in the same oil, place it on the tomatoes, cover with the remaining tomatoes and the sauce, then bake for 20 minutes at 180 °C covered, and 10 minutes uncovered.
Serve immediately, sprinkled with parsley or coriander if desired.
poisson-frit-liberien: Clean the fish, rinse it and pat it dry.
Mix the flour with the paprika, garlic powder and onion powder.
Dip each piece of fish in the buttermilk, then coat it in the flour, pressing firmly.
Fry the fish for 3 to 4 minutes per side in hot oil until golden, then drain on kitchen paper. Serve with a green salad.
poisson-epice-a-la-sindhi: Fry the fish for 3 minutes on one side in the oil, then turn it over so the golden side faces down in an ovenproof dish.
Mix the Greek yoghurt, finely sliced onions, fresh coriander, ground coriander, cumin, salt and tamarind paste.
Spread the yoghurt mixture over the fish.
Bake for 15 minutes at 200 °C until the top is golden, then serve with wholemeal bread.
poitrine-de-b-uf-epicee-rotie: Brown the beef brisket in hot vegetable oil on all sides.
Add the onion and celery and cook over a medium heat until softened, then stir in the garlic, cumin, pepper, mustard, oregano, salt and tomatoes.
Pour in the stock, vinegar, sugar and bay leaf, cover and simmer over a low heat for 2 hours, adding water if needed.
Add the red pepper 30 minutes before the end of cooking, then serve the meat with the pepper and the sauce.
poitrine-de-porc-braisee-rouge: Melt the sugar in the oil over a high heat until it forms a caramel.
Add the pork belly cubes and brown them.
Lower the heat, add the stock, ginger, star anise, soy sauce and rice wine, then cover and simmer for 40 minutes, stirring from time to time.
Remove the lid, add the spring onion and reduce the sauce until it is thick and glossy.
Serve with brown rice and a green salad.
porc-et-haricots-de-lima-a-la-poele: Cook the lima beans according to the packet, without salt, then drain.
Brown the pork chops over a medium heat, then remove them and keep only one tablespoon of the cooking juices.
Add the stock to the pork, the flour and the basil, then pour in 750 ml of water and stir until thickened.
Add the beans to the pan, then arrange the pork chops on top, cover and cook for 5 minutes over a low heat.
Serve with brown rice and a tomato salad.
porc-laque: Prick the pork shoulder strips with a fork, then coat them in the marinade and cover with cling film.
Leave to marinate in the fridge for several hours, ideally overnight.
Preheat the oven to 230 °C, line a dish with foil and arrange the meat in a single layer without stacking it.
Roast for 20 minutes, brushing the marinade on at least twice, until you have a nicely lacquered crust.
Leave the meat to rest, then serve with wholegrain rice and a tomato salad.
porc-vapeur-aux-feuilles-de-moutarde: Blanch the mustard greens for 2 min in boiling water, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Mix the cornflour, sugar, soy sauce and white wine, then add the sliced pork and leave to marinate for 20 min.
Heat the oil in a wok, stir-fry the black bean sauce for 1 min, then add the pork and toss for 2 min.
Add the mustard greens and the water, simmer for 4 to 5 min, season with pepper and serve.
pork-aachi: Brown the pork in half of the coconut oil, add half of the garam masala and fry for 1 min.
Add the vinegar, fry for 1 min, then pour in 250 ml of water and cook until the meat is half cooked.
Fry the thinly sliced onion and chopped chilli with the remaining coconut oil over a medium heat, then add the garlic and ginger after 4 min.
Stir in the remaining garam masala, add the pork stock and a little water, then cook for 4 min over a low heat, stirring.

Add the half-cooked meat, cook over a medium heat until fully cooked, then stir in the potato purée diluted in a little water. Remove from the heat, leave to rest for 3 to 5 min and serve with tomatoes in salad.
posho-et-haricots: Fry the thinly sliced onion in the vegetable oil over a high heat until it begins to turn golden.
Add the tomato, curry powder, ginger and cumin, and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the cooked white beans, season, and simmer gently for 10 minutes, stirring.
Bring the water to the boil, pour in the maize flour in a steady stream while stirring, then cook for 5 minutes, turning continuously.
Serve the posho straight away with the beans.
potage-aux-lentilles-corail: Heat the olive oil, then fry the sliced onion, crushed garlic and carrots in rounds.
Add the red lentils, the vegetable stock, the thyme, salt and pepper.
Bring to the boil, then cook for 30 minutes in a pressure cooker.
Blend the soup until smooth and creamy, then serve hot.
poularde-aux-morilles: Soak the morels in water for 2 hours, then cook them for 30 minutes in salted, peppered water at a gentle simmer.
Brown the chicken pieces in the oil for 5 to 10 minutes, then season with salt and pepper.
Deglaze with the vin jaune, cover and cook over a medium heat for about 50 minutes until the wine has reduced by two thirds.
Drain the morels, add them to the casserole with the crème fraîche and simmer for 10 minutes.
Serve with tagliatelle or fresh pasta and a tomato salad.
poulet-dg: Cut the chicken into small pieces and marinate it with the Honig stock cubes and the finely chopped basil.
Blanch the sliced onion in the hot oil, then brown the chicken, turning it over.
Cover and simmer for 5 min, then add the deseeded tomato and garlic, and let it simmer over a low heat.
Fry the peeled plantains in thick slices, then add the diced pepper and carrot to the sauce, season with salt and pepper.
Mix the fried plantains into the sauce and serve hot.
poulet-au-beurre-indien: Cut the chicken into small cubes, then mix with the tandoori masala, Greek yoghurt and lemon juice. Massage by hand and leave to rest for at least 30 min.
Melt the butter in a large frying pan, add the thinly sliced onion and fry until soft and lightly golden.
Add the garlic, ginger, turmeric, coriander and chilli, then sauté over a medium heat.
Add the marinated chicken and cook until it turns white, without overcooking it. Stir in the tomato purée, then the cream and let it heat through.
Cover and simmer for 10 min. Serve with brown rice and a tomato salad on the side.
poulet-au-beurre-style-cape-malay: Mix the Greek yoghurt, oil, ginger and garlic paste, half of the lemon juice and the spices, then brush over the chicken halves and leave to marinate for a few hours.
Grill the chicken until it is nicely golden, or cook it in a frying pan over a medium heat until fully cooked through.
Melt the butter with the tomato purée and the remaining lemon juice, add the leftover marinade, bring to the boil, then leave to simmer for a few minutes.
Remove from the heat, stir in the double cream, arrange the chicken on a serving dish, spoon the sauce over and garnish with mint. Serve with brown rice and a tomato salad.
poulet-au-curry: Cut the chicken into 5 to 7 cm pieces, score the edges, then marinate them for 8 hours in the fridge with the garlic, Greek yoghurt, coriander, garam masala, chilli and pepper.
Fry the thinly sliced onion, green chillies and chopped tomato in olive oil over a low heat until the onion is light golden.
Add the remaining garam masala, the chilli powder and the ground cashew nuts, then fry the chicken for 5 minutes, stirring gently.
Add the marinade and enough water to cover the chicken, then leave to simmer over a low to medium heat for 30 to 45 minutes.
Remove from the heat, leave to rest for a few minutes, then serve with basmati rice.
poulet-au-gingembre-et-cardamome: Blend the peeled ginger with the garlic, ground almonds and water.
Cut the chicken into cubes and fry it in the oil for 7 to 8 min.
In the same pan, fry the sliced onion with the cardamom for 10 min, then remove the cardamom.
Add the ginger paste and the cumin, then stir in the yoghurt little by little and cook for 10 min over a low heat with the chicken.
Serve with rice cooked in water and vegetables on the side.
poulet-au-paprika: Fry the thinly sliced onion for 3 to 4 minutes in the olive oil until it turns golden.
Add the chicken, black pepper, salt and paprika, stir well, then cover with water.
Simmer gently over a low heat for 45 to 50 minutes, stirring from time to time and without letting it boil, until the chicken is tender and the juices have almost disappeared.
Stir the crème fraîche and single cream into the juices, then sprinkle with chopped parsley.
Serve with wholegrain rice and green beans.
poulet-barbecue: Mix the stock, garlic, lemon, brown sugar and salt, then marinate the chicken in the fridge for 2 hours.
Reduce the tomato purée, honey, cider vinegar and Worcestershire sauce by half over medium-high heat.
Rub the chicken with the mixture of paprika, rosemary, thyme, cayenne pepper and brown sugar, then leave to rest in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Grill the chicken for 10 minutes on a preheated charcoal barbecue, turning often, then brush with sauce until it reaches 165 °C at the core for the breast and 170 °C for the thigh.
Cover with foil and leave to rest for 7 minutes, then serve with the remaining sauce. Serve with brown rice and a tomato salad.
poulet-barbecue-de-jardin: Mix the dry spices and rub them over the chicken, then refrigerate for 1 hour.
Reduce the tomato purée, honey and cider vinegar by half over a medium heat for about 10 minutes.
Grill the chicken over a medium heat for 15 to 20 minutes, turning often and brushing with sauce at each turn, until cooked through.
Leave to rest for 10 minutes, then serve with brown rice and steamed green beans.
poulet-de-janze-a-la-normande: Poulet de Janzé à la normande
Brown the chicken pieces in the butter and oil, then set aside to keep warm.
Colour the thinly sliced onions in the wiped casserole dish, add the chicken, flambé with calvados, then pour in the cider.
Leave to simmer for 1 hour 30 minutes, set the chicken aside, reduce the juices with the crème fraîche, then return the chicken to heat through.
Serve piping hot with brown rice and green beans.
poulet-roti-sur-lit-de-sel: Roast chicken on a bed of salt
Stuff the chicken with the lemon cut into quarters, the garlic cloves and the rosemary.
Tie the chicken so that it keeps its shape.
Spread the salt in an ovenproof dish and place the chicken on top.
Roast for 90 min at 190 °C until the flesh is tender and the skin crisp, then serve with the brown rice and the green salad.
poulet-teriyaki-a-l-ananas: Bring the rice to the boil with water and a pinch of salt, cover and cook for 20 min over a low heat.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan or wok over a high heat.
Stir-fry the chicken for 5 min, then add the onion and red pepper and cook for 3 min.
Add the pineapple and teriyaki sauce, let reduce for 2 min, then serve over the rice.
poulet-a-l-orange-epinards-et-tomates-ce: Orange chicken, spinach and cherry tomatoes
Preheat the oven to 200 °C and place a baking tray inside to heat up.
Mix the garlic, orange zest, salt and pepper, then coat the chicken pieces in the mixture.
Lay the spinach on a square of aluminium foil, add the chicken and the lightly oiled cherry tomatoes, then fold the foil up into a parcel.
Bake the parcels for 15 minutes on the hot tray, then let them rest for 5 minutes before serving with a handful of wholemeal bread.
poulet-a-la-comtoise: Brown the raw chicken pieces on all sides in olive oil in a casserole dish, then season with salt and pepper.
Deglaze with the white wine, season with nutmeg, then bake for 30 min at 240 °C.
Mix the cooking juices, egg yolks, crème fraîche and grated comté, then let simmer for 15 min.
Pour the sauce into a gravy boat and serve with the chicken, sautéed potatoes and tagliatelle.
poulet-epice-a-la-creme-fraiche: Heat the oil in a frying pan until it is very hot but not smoking.
Add the cardamom, coriander, cinnamon, cumin and bay leaf, then cook for 1 to 2 minutes until the seeds crackle.
Lower the heat, add the garlic and onion, and cook until soft and translucent, then set aside.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper, dust it with flour, then brown it in the pan until almost cooked through.
Return the reserved onion and the raisins to the pan, add the crème fraîche and simmer until the chicken is tender and the sauce has reduced. Serve with almonds and coconut.
poelee-d-aubergine-et-pois-chiches: Fry the red pepper and garlic in the olive oil over a medium heat for a few minutes.
Add the mushrooms and aubergine and cook for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Pour in the tomatoes, chickpeas and tarragon, cover and leave to simmer for 10 to 12 minutes.
Stir in the basil and broccoli, continue for 8 to 10 minutes with the lid partly on, season with salt and pepper, and serve.
pates-au-poulet-et-citron: Season the chicken with salt, pepper and oregano, then dust it with flour, shaking off the excess.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over a high heat and sear the chicken for 1 to 2 minutes per side, then set aside.
Caramelise the lemon slices for 1 minute per side in the same pan.
Add the artichoke, tomato, garlic, capers and chilli, toss for 2 minutes, then pour in the white wine and let it reduce.
Return the chicken to the pan with the cream and rosemary, add the cooked pasta and spinach, and toss for 1 minute until the spinach wilts. Serve immediately.
pates-au-thon: Finely chop the onion and cook it gently in a little olive oil until it is translucent.
Add the crushed chilli and the drained tuna, then cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in the tomato passata and simmer gently until the pasta is cooked.
Cook the penne according to the packet instructions, drain, then toss with the tuna sauce. Season with salt, pepper and parmesan. Serve with green beans.
pate-chinois: Boil the peeled potatoes cut into quarters for 15 min in salted boiling water, then drain and mash them with the milk using a pestle.
Fry the chopped onion in the butter, add the minced beef and cook until it loses its pink colour, then season with salt and pepper.
Spread the meat in a small ovenproof dish and cover with drained sweetcorn.
Top with the mash, then bake for 25 min at 190 °C until the top is golden.
porkolt: Cut the beef into cubes, and the onion and garlic into small pieces.
Melt the fat in a casserole dish, fry the onion until golden brown, then add the meat, garlic, pepper, salt and cumin and fry over a high heat.
Take off the heat, add the sweet paprika, stir, then return to a low heat with the tomato and pepper cut into pieces and a little water.
Leave to simmer uncovered for at least 3 hours, adding a little water if needed, until the meat is tender.
Serve with pasta, gnocchi or potatoes.
ragout-d-agneau-a-la-irlandaise: Brown the lamb pieces in a large saucepan over a medium heat, then remove them.
Sauté the pepper, mushrooms, carrots, celery and onion in the olive oil over a high heat.
Add the sautéed vegetables, the stock, the lamb, the potatoes and the dill salt to a large pot.
Cover and cook for 30 minutes over a medium-high heat, stirring from time to time, then reduce the heat and simmer covered for 1 hour 30 to 2 hours.
ragout-de-betterave-et-chou: Cook the meat and bones in a large saucepan with the tomatoes and an equal quantity of water, bring to the boil, then leave to simmer for 1 h to 1 h 30.
Add the cabbage, garlic, carrots, onion and celery, then cook until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the cooked beetroot cut into cubes and mix.
Season, adjust to taste, cook for 5 more minutes, then serve with potatoes.
ragout-de-b-uf-au-piment-vert: Heat the vegetable oil in a sauté pan, brown the minced beef on all sides, then transfer it to a casserole dish.
Fry the sliced onion in the sauté pan until golden, then add the chopped garlic for 2 minutes.
Pour the onion and garlic into the casserole dish, then add the potatoes, chilli, celery, sweetcorn, oregano and 3 to 4 glasses of water.
Bring to the boil, reduce the heat and leave to simmer for 1 to 1.5 hours until the meat is very tender.
ragout-de-b-uf-et-orge: Lightly flour the minced beef, then brown it in the vegetable oil.
Add the sliced onion, garlic and celery, then sweat briefly.
Pour in the vegetable stock, tomato purée, thyme, marjoram and Worcestershire sauce, then leave to simmer for 1 hour 30 minutes.
Add the pearl barley and leave to simmer for 30 minutes.
Add the potatoes, mushrooms, green beans and carrot, then cook for 1 hour. Sprinkle with chopped parsley before serving.
ragout-de-b-uf-zambien: Heat the vegetable oil over a medium heat in a large saucepan.
Fry the chopped onion and the finely sliced garlic until soft and translucent.
Add the minced beef and brown it on all sides.
Pour in the vegetable stock or water, add the carrot, potato, tomato and peppers, then season with paprika, cayenne pepper, cumin, coriander and salt.
Simmer gently for 1 hour to 1 hour 30 minutes, stirring from time to time, then serve with wholegrain rice and a green salad.
ragout-de-b-uf-a-la-mijoteuse: Trim the fat from the meat and cut it into cubes if necessary.
Put all the ingredients into the slow cooker with salt and pepper, then mix well.
Cover and cook for 12 hours on low or 5 to 6 hours on high.
Remove the bay leaves, then serve.
ragout-de-lapin-maltais-stuffat-tal-fene: Cut the rabbit into 10 to 12 pieces, keeping the offal aside.
Fry the finely chopped garlic in the oil, then sear the rabbit pieces until cooked through without over-browning them.
In a large saucepan, add the rabbit, the potatoes in large chunks, the carrot, the tomatoes, the wine, the sugar, the bay leaf, salt, pepper, spices and Tabasco.
Cover and simmer over a low heat for 4 hours, stirring from time to time during the first hour.
Add the peas for the last 10 minutes of cooking, then serve.
ragout-de-patates-douces-mais-et-haricot: Sweet potato, sweetcorn and bean stew
Fry the finely chopped onion and garlic in the vegetable oil over a medium heat until translucent.
Add the diced tomato and the cubed potatoes, then cover with water.
Bring to the boil, reduce the heat and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Add the sweetcorn and white beans, season with salt and pepper, and simmer for 5 to 10 minutes.
Serve hot, scattered with fresh coriander.
ragout-de-pois-chiches-au-safran: Fry the onion, pepper, garlic, saffron and potatoes in the olive oil for 15 minutes over a medium heat.
Add the paprika, then the white wine, and let it reduce for 1 minute.
Add the chickpeas, tomatoes, stock, salt and pepper, and bring to the boil.
Reduce the heat and cook covered for 30 to 40 minutes until the potatoes are tender, then leave to rest for 15 minutes.
Serve the stew around the rice, garnished with parsley.
ragout-de-poisson-zambien: Heat the vegetable oil over a medium heat in a large saucepan, then fry the finely chopped onion and garlic until soft.
Add the tomato, red pepper and chilli, and cook until the vegetables are tender.
Pour in the fish stock and bring to a simmer, then gently add the pieces of fish.
Season with the cayenne pepper, paprika, cumin, coriander and salt, cover and leave to simmer for 15 to 20 minutes until the fish flakes apart.
Adjust the seasoning, leave to rest for a few minutes and serve with brown rice.
ragout-de-poulet-aux-haricots-a-il-noir: Cook the black-eyed beans for 20 min in unsalted simmering water, then drain.
Sweat the onion, carrot and celery in the oil for 5 min.
Add the garlic, ginger, salt and pepper, then sweat for 2 min.
Stir in the rice and stock, add the tomato and bring to the boil.
Add the beans, chicken and curry, then simmer gently for 35 min until the rice is tender.
ragout-des-trois-s-urs: Fry the sliced onion in the olive oil over a low heat for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and continue until golden.
Add the pepper, the tomatoes, the pinto beans, the sweetcorn, the stock, the chilli, the cumin and the oregano, then leave to simmer covered for 20 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper, then scatter over the chopped coriander before serving.
ragout-irlandais: Layer the lamb, onion, carrot and potato in a lidded casserole, starting and finishing with the potato.
Pour in the water, season with salt and pepper, and scatter over the chopped parsley.
Cover and cook over a very low heat for about 2 hours 30 minutes, until the meat is tender and the potatoes have thickened the juices.
ragout-liberien-a-l-aubergine: Heat the palm oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat, then fry the chopped onion and finely sliced garlic until soft.
Add the meat in pieces and brown it on all sides.
Pour in the chicken stock, then add the tomato, red pepper and diced aubergine, and leave to simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring from time to time.
Season with pepper and salt, leave to rest for a few minutes, then serve with brown rice.
rajma-curry-de-haricots-rouges-sindhi: Rajma, Sindhi-style red kidney bean curry
Soak the red kidney beans overnight, then drain.
Cover the beans with water, add the bicarbonate of soda and cook at a rolling boil for 30 min until tender, then drain, reserving 100 g of the cooking water.
Fry the onion in the oil, then add the tomato and chilli until the oil separates.
Add the beans and the reserved cooking water, cook for 5 to 10 min, season with salt and add chilli powder.
Off the heat, stir in the garam masala and serve hot with white rice.
rakott-krumpli-gratin-de-pommes-de-terre: Boil the potatoes for 15 to 20 minutes in salted water, then peel them and cut them into slices.
Shell the hard-boiled eggs and slice them.
Grease an ovenproof dish and arrange the potatoes, eggs and salt in alternating layers.
Drizzle with olive oil, spread soured cream over the top and bake for 35 minutes at 200 °C.
Serve hot with a green salad and a tomato salad.
ravioles-au-crabe-et-langoustine: Flake the crab meat, add the finely chopped chervil and 5 cl of cream, season with pepper and mix.
Mark 3 cm squares on the pasta sheet, place a small spoonful of the crab mixture on each square, brush with egg white and seal with the second square.
Press the edges, trim with a pastry wheel, then cook the ravioli for 2 minutes in salted boiling water.
Sauté the langoustines for 3 minutes in olive oil, season with salt and pepper, then remove them.
Pour in the remaining cream with the pink peppercorns and thyme, heat through, return the langoustines, then serve with the drained ravioli and a tomato salad.
risotto-au-poulet: Fry the thinly sliced onion in a heavy-bottomed casserole, add the chicken breast cut into strips and sear until golden.
Pour in the white wine, add the chopped tomato and leave to simmer for 10 minutes over a low heat.
Stir in the rice and cook for 2 minutes, then add the hot stock a little at a time until fully absorbed, and season with salt and pepper.
Transfer to a serving dish and sprinkle with chopped parsley.
risotto-de-saumon: Fry the chopped onion in olive oil for 5 min.
Add the rice and stir until it becomes glossy, then pour in the white wine.
Add the fish stock a ladle at a time, stirring until fully absorbed.
Add the diced salmon and cook for 5 min, then stir in the grated parmesan.
Leave to rest for a few minutes and serve.
riz-complet-saute-a-la-dinde-hachee: Sautéed Brown Rice with Minced Turkey
Brown the minced turkey in a non-stick pan with the lemon pepper and allspice, crumbling it as it cooks.
Add the diced tomatoes and stir until the turkey is thoroughly cooked, about 10 minutes.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok, then add the cooked rice and heat it through evenly.
Pour the teriyaki sauce over the rice, toss, add the turkey and mix well before serving.
riz-jollof-liberien: Season the chicken with salt and chilli powder, then leave to rest for 5 min.
Brown the chicken in hot vegetable oil, then transfer it to a large saucepan.
Fry the onion and pork in the same pan, then add them to the saucepan.
Add the tomato purée, stock, vegetables and rinsed rice, stir, then cook over a low heat for 40 min.
Serve hot with a side of salad vegetables.
riz-saute-au-hamburger: Heat the rapeseed oil in a non-stick frying pan, then fry the garlic, red onion, ginger and chilli for 2 minutes, stirring.
Add the minced beef and cook until well browned and cooked through.
Stir in the celery and spring onions, then add the rice, soy sauce, salt and pepper.
Cook, stirring, until the rice is piping hot and evenly mixed, then serve straight away.
rocoto-relleno: Cut the tops off the chillies, remove the veins and seeds, then blanch them twice for 3 minutes each in salted water.
Blanch them a third time in sweetened water to soften the heat.
Brown the chopped onion with the salt and cumin, then add the meat, oregano, parsley, olives and egg.
Stuff the chillies, cover with their tops, add the potatoes and cheese, then bake for 15 minutes at 360°C.
rolex-ougandais-omelette-roulee-au-chapa: Rolex, Ugandan egg and chapati roll
Beat the eggs in a bowl with the onion, tomato, cabbage, coriander, salt and black pepper.
Heat 1 tbsp of oil in a frying pan over a medium heat and pour in half of the mixture.
Cook for 3 minutes until the top is barely wet, then place a chapati on top.
Flip the omelette so the chapati is underneath, leave to heat for 2 minutes, then roll the omelette up with the chapati on the outside.
Wrap in foil and serve immediately, repeating with the rest of the mixture and chapati.
rougail-de-morue: Desalt the cod by poaching it in water for 10 minutes, repeating the process 2 or 3 times, then flake it, removing the bones.
Finely chop the onion, mince the garlic, peel and deseed the tomatoes, and prepare the chillies.
Heat the oil, then fry the onion and garlic for 2 to 3 minutes without burning them, add the chillies for 2 to 3 minutes, then add the tomatoes, thyme and turmeric.
Simmer everything for 4 to 6 minutes, stirring, then add the flaked cod and 2 glasses of water.
Simmer for 15 minutes, taste and adjust the salt, and serve with wholegrain rice and green beans.
rouleaux-de-poulet-a-l-italienne: Mix the ricotta, cream cheese and half the mozzarella, then set aside.
Flatten the chicken breasts between two sheets of cling film to 5 mm thick.
Season one side of the chicken with salt and pepper, spread the cheese mixture over the other side, then roll up.
Arrange the rolls, seam side down, in a greased dish, spoon over the coulis and bake for 20 min at 220 °C.
Sprinkle over the remaining mozzarella and place under the grill until melted, then serve hot with wholewheat rice and a tomato salad.
salade-d-asperges-grillees-aux-pois-chic: Trim the ends of the asparagus, snap them in half and rinse them, then season with the salt and 1 tbsp of oil.
Heat a non-stick frying pan over a high heat, grill the asparagus for about 5 minutes, then transfer them to a salad bowl.
Fry the garlic and the drained capers for 2 minutes in 2 tbsp of oil, then pour this mixture over the asparagus.
Add the drained chickpeas and the lemon juice, toss together, then mix in the chopped parsley and mint.
Add the washed and dried baby spinach, toss and serve.
salade-de-pommes-et-pois-chiches: In a salad bowl, mix the chickpeas, the chopped apples, the onion and the celery.
In a bowl, whisk together the lemon juice, olive oil, chives, basil, salt and pepper.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss well.
Leave to marinate in the fridge for a few moments before serving.
salade-de-riz-au-thon: Cook the rice in boiling salted water, then drain it and leave it to cool.
Cut the tomatoes into pieces and the hard-boiled eggs into quarters.
Mix the rice, drained tuna, sweetcorn, tomatoes and eggs with the mayonnaise in a salad bowl.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve chilled.
salade-nicoise: Cut the tomatoes into quarters, lightly salt them, then drain.
Thinly slice the cucumber, onion, red pepper and artichokes, and cook the broad beans for 5 min in simmering salted water.
Mix the drained tuna, the vegetables, the quartered hard-boiled eggs and the black olives in a salad bowl rubbed with garlic.
Prepare a dressing with the olive oil, chopped basil, salt and pepper, pour it over the salad and serve well chilled.
sandwich-a-l-avocat-et-au-tofu: Halve the avocados, remove the stones, then cut one half into quarters and place a quarter on each slice of bread.
Mash the avocado with a fork with a little olive oil and season with salt.
Top one slice of tomato with sliced tomato and the other with tofu, season both halves with salt, then close the sandwich.
sauce-gombo-au-b-uf: Wash the okra, trim the ends and slice into rounds. Season the meat with salt, pepper and spices.
Heat the palm oil over a medium heat, then fry the onion and garlic for 3 minutes until they turn translucent.
Add the meat and brown it on all sides, then stir in the tomatoes, tomato purée, nutmeg, ginger and paprika.
Add the okra, stir and cover. Leave to simmer over a low heat for 30 minutes, adding a little water if needed, then adjust the seasoning.
Scatter over chopped coriander and serve hot with wholegrain rice.
saumon-au-miel-et-a-la-moutarde: Preheat the oven to 180 °C, gas mark 6.
Rinse and pat dry the salmon, remove the bones, then cut it into portions.
Mix the honey and mustard, and adjust the seasoning to taste.
Spread the mixture generously over and under the salmon.
Place on the upper shelf for 15 to 18 minutes, then finish under the grill for 2 to 3 minutes without letting it caramelise. Serve with wholegrain rice and green beans.
saute-de-b-uf-au-miel-et-au-sesame: Fry the onion and garlic in the groundnut oil until the garlic is golden, then set aside.
Season the minced beef with salt and pepper, then brown it over a high heat in two batches.
Add the chilli, carrot, soy sauce, honey, vinegar and spring onions, and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Return the onion, garlic and beef to the wok, and toss until heated through.
Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds and serve with brown rice.
saute-de-b-uf-aux-poivrons: Season the minced beef with salt and freshly ground black pepper, then set aside.
Heat a frying pan or wok over medium-high heat, add the groundnut oil and sear the meat for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring until browned.
Add the sliced pepper, garlic and chilli and fry for 3 minutes until the edges of the vegetables are lightly golden.
Return the meat to the pan, add the soy sauce and heat for 1 minute. Serve hot.
saute-de-joues-de-fletan: Heat the groundnut oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Fry the halibut cheeks, stirring, until they start to brown.
Add the carrot, celery, ginger and garlic, then keep stirring.
Pour in the soy sauce and fish stock, bring to a simmer, garnish with spring onion and serve with brown rice and green beans.
saute-de-poulet-au-curcuma-et-aux-asperg: Mix the flour, turmeric and salt, then coat the chicken pieces.
Brown the chicken for 8 min in hot coconut oil over medium-high heat.
Add the sliced asparagus, season with salt and cook for 2 min, keeping a little bite.
Pour in the honey diluted in water, add pepper and simmer for 2 min until thickened.
Off the heat, stir in the rice vinegar and lime juice, adjust the seasoning and serve.
sega-wat-ragout-de-b-uf-epice-ethiopien: Sega wat, Ethiopian spiced beef stew
Heat the olive oil in a large casserole dish over a medium heat, then fry the thinly sliced onion until translucent.
Add the crushed garlic and cook for 1 minute, then stir in the berbere, tomato purée, paprika, cumin and turmeric.
Add the minced beef and brown for 5 minutes, stirring, then pour in the stock and bring to the boil.
Reduce the heat, cover and simmer for 25 minutes, stirring from time to time, then adjust the seasoning to taste.
Scatter over the finely chopped parsley and serve with a wholegrain cereal to accompany the sauce.
shakshuka-bil-lahm-a-la-viande-hachee: Shakshuka bil lahm, with minced beef
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan and fry the finely chopped onion and garlic until translucent.
Add the minced beef and brown it, then stir in the diced pepper and tomatoes.
Season with the cumin, paprika, salt and pepper, cover and simmer over a low heat for 15 minutes.
Make small wells in the sauce, crack the eggs into them, cover and cook for 5 minutes.
Scatter over the chopped parsley and serve.
sharmoula-bil-lahm-viande-marinee-libyen: Sharmoula bil lahm, Libyan marinated meat
Mix the garlic, olive oil, lemon juice, cumin, paprika, coriander and cayenne pepper, then season with salt and pepper.
Coat the minced beef in this marinade, then cover and refrigerate for 2 to 4 hours.
Preheat the grill to medium-high, then shape the meat into skewers, leaving a small gap between each piece.
Grill the skewers for 10 to 15 minutes, turning them and brushing with the remaining marinade, then garnish with chopped parsley and serve with a slice of wholemeal bread and a green salad.
shawarma-d-agneau: Cut the lamb into large 4 cm chunks, then mix in nutmeg, cinnamon, cardamom, crushed garlic, cayenne pepper, lemon juice and vinegar.
Pour the marinade over the meat and leave to rest for at least 2 hours.
Grill the thinly sliced onions with a little garlic for a few minutes.
Drain the meat, pat it dry, then grill it until golden.
Serve with wholemeal pitta bread, fresh onions and a green salad.
shorba-bil-lahm-soupe-libyenne-a-l-agnea: Shorba bil lahm, Libyan lamb soup
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat, then fry the finely chopped onion and garlic until translucent.
Add the lamb cubes and brown them on all sides.
Stir in the cumin, coriander, turmeric, cayenne pepper, salt and pepper, then toast for 1 minute.
Add the diced carrot, potato and tomato, stir, pour in the stock and bring to the boil.
Reduce the heat, cover and simmer for about 1 hour until the meat is tender, then adjust the seasoning and serve hot, sprinkled with chopped parsley.
short-ribs-coreennes: Whisk together the soy sauce, spring onions, garlic, sesame oil, rapeseed oil and chilli until you have a smooth marinade.
Coat the meat in the marinade, then refrigerate overnight.
Preheat the barbecue to 110 °C and cook the covered meat for 5 hours, until it pulls away from the bone.
skillet-hamburger-aux-pates: Cook the pasta for 10 min in boiling salted, oiled water, then drain.
Brown the minced beef in a frying pan with the garlic salt and chopped onion.
Add the tomato and leave to cook for 1 to 2 min.
Stir in the drained pasta and serve.
sliders-au-chipotle: Spread the minced beef into thin patties on baking paper, then cut 8 steaks per tray.
Season the steaks with salt, pepper, chipotle powder and garlic powder.
Cook the steaks on a plancha at 180 °C, 2 min per side, adding the cheese at the end.
Toast the small buns, spread with minced chipotle mayonnaise, top with a steak and serve hot with a green salad and tomatoes.
smore-ragout-de-b-uf-eurasien: Cut the beef into pieces, mix with the bicarbonate of soda, sugar, vinegar and soy sauce, then leave to marinate for 30 min.
Blend the onion and garlic, and soak the carrots and potatoes in water.
Fry the blended onion and garlic, the ginger and cinnamon in the oil until the onion is golden and fragrant.
Add the marinated beef and fry until it changes colour, then pour in water and simmer until the meat is tender.
Add the carrots for 5 min, then the potatoes until tender, add the tomato and garnish with coriander before serving.
souffle-au-bleu-de-gex: Prepare the buttered soufflé dish, then melt the butter in a saucepan and stir in the flour to make a roux.
Add the milk and bring to the boil, then remove from the heat and gradually stir in the Bleu de Gex until melted.
Mix the egg yolk into the mixture, then whisk the egg whites until stiff and fold them in gently.
Fill the dish and bake for 20 minutes at 200 °C, then serve piping hot straight from the oven.
soupe-au-poivre-liberienne: Heat the palm oil over a medium heat in a large saucepan, then fry the onion, garlic and ginger until the onion is translucent.
Add the chilli and bay leaf, cook for a few minutes, then brown the chicken on all sides.
Pour in the stock, bring to a simmer, cover and cook the chicken for 20 to 25 minutes.
Add the fish, sliced plantain and carrot, continue cooking for about 10 minutes, then season with salt and pepper.
Serve with carrots and green beans on the side.
soupe-aux-cacahuetes-ghaneenne-nkatenkwa: Place the chicken, whole onions, tomatoes, ginger, bay leaf, chilli and stock in a saucepan, bring to the boil, then leave to simmer until the chicken is tender.
Loosen the peanut butter with a little water in another saucepan, then add the rest of the water and leave to simmer for 20 minutes.
Remove the onions and tomatoes, blend them finely, then return them to the soup and leave to simmer for 5 minutes.
Pour the peanut sauce into the soup, add the okra and leave to simmer for 15 minutes, then season with salt and chilli.
Serve with fufu or a side of your choice.
soupe-aux-haricots: Pour the vegetable stock and water into a large casserole, then bring to a high heat.
Add the frozen vegetables, the chopped tomatoes and the pasta, cover and bring to the boil.
Rinse and drain the red and black beans.
Add the beans, the Italian herbs and the garlic powder, then cook for 5 minutes over a medium heat, stirring.
Reduce the heat, add the Parmesan, leave to simmer for 5 minutes and serve immediately.
soupe-cremeuse-aux-tomates-et-haricots-b: Creamy tomato and white bean soup
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat, then fry the chopped onion with salt and pepper for 2 minutes.
Add the white beans with their liquid, the garlic, oregano and sage, and leave to simmer for 3 to 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes, tomato purée, chilli and water, and leave to simmer for 5 to 10 minutes, stirring.
Remove from the heat, add the cream cheese, blend the soup with a hand blender, then cook over a very low heat for 10 minutes.
Add the basil at the end of cooking, and serve the soup piping hot with a few basil leaves as garnish.
soupe-d-asperges-champignons-mais-et-pou: Asparagus, mushroom, sweetcorn and chicken soup
Poach the chicken escalopes in simmering water until they are cooked through and quite white, then shred them finely.
Fry the chopped onion and garlic in butter, then add the drained mushrooms and the sweetcorn.
Add the chopped asparagus, the cooking water and the shredded chicken, then season with salt, sugar and pepper.
Leave to simmer for 20 minutes without blending, then serve with wholemeal bread.
soupe-de-b-uf-et-legumes: Place the sliced onion and vegetables in a large saucepan, then add the minced beef.
Leave to simmer over a low heat for 30 min, stirring well.
Once the meat and vegetables are cooked, add the vegetable stock and salt.
Bring back to a gentle simmer and serve with a slice of wholemeal bread.
soupe-de-champignons-au-tofu: Blend the tofu with 60 ml of water for 2 min until smooth, then add the remaining water and blend again.
Fry the finely chopped onion for 5 min in a large frying pan.
Add the sliced mushrooms and thyme, and sauté for 5 min.
Pour in the white wine and let it simmer for 5 min.
Stir in the tofu mixture and the soy sauce, and let it simmer until the mushrooms soften. Season with salt to taste. Serve with a slice of wholemeal bread.
soupe-de-cotes-de-porc-bah-kut-teh: Soak the dried mushrooms in 240 ml of boiling water, then slice them into strips once softened, keeping the liquid.
