Blanch the pork ribs in cold water until the scum rises, then rinse and drain.
Place the pork, garlic, ginseng, mushrooms and their liquid in a saucepan, then cover with cold water.
Put the cinnamon, star anise and peppercorns in a muslin bag, bring to the boil, then leave to simmer for 45 to 60 minutes, skimming as you go.
Season with salt, pepper, sugar and soy sauce at the end of cooking, then serve the soup piping hot.
soupe-de-feuilles-de-manioc-liberienne: Wash the cassava leaves, remove the tough stems, then chop them finely.
Heat the palm oil over a medium heat and fry the onion, garlic and ginger until the onion is translucent.
Add the chilli and the meat, brown on all sides, then pour in the stock and simmer for 20 minutes with the lid on.
Add the sweet potato and plantain, cook for 10 minutes, then stir in the cassava leaves and simmer for 45 minutes, stirring from time to time.
Season with salt and pepper, and let it rest for a few minutes before serving.
soupe-de-haricots-blancs-au-basilic-et-a: White bean soup with basil and rosemary
Finely blend the drained white beans, chicken stock, tomato passata, garlic, basil, rosemary and chilli flakes until smooth.
Pour the soup into a large saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer.
Leave to simmer partially covered for 4 to 5 min, stirring often to bring out the flavours.
Serve the hot soup with garlic croutons.
soupe-de-haricots-blancs-aux-feuilles-de: White bean soup with pumpkin leaves
Soak the white beans for several hours, then drain and rinse them.
Bring the beans to the boil in water, reduce the heat and simmer for 30 minutes until they begin to soften.
Add the pumpkin leaves, peppers, onion, garlic, chilli, stock, crayfish and chilli oil, then season with salt and pepper.
Simmer for 30 to 60 minutes until the beans are tender and the soup is nicely thick, then serve.
soupe-de-lentilles: Fry the red lentils for 2 min in hot sunflower oil.
Add the chopped celery, carrots and onion, then simmer for 5 min over a low heat.
Pour in the stock, bring to the boil, then cook for 20 min over a low heat until the vegetables are tender.
Blend roughly, stir in the lemon juice, season with salt and pepper and serve hot.
soupe-de-lentilles-rouges: Rinse the lentils and pick through them to remove any impurities.
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat, then fry the onion and carrot for a few minutes.
Add the garlic, lentils, bay leaf and stock, then leave to simmer for 20 to 30 minutes over a medium-low heat.
soupe-de-lentilles-orge-et-tomate: Sweat the finely sliced onion in the butter until soft.
Add the lentils, barley and water, then cook until the lentils are tender.
Add the deseeded, diced tomato towards the end of cooking.
Blend the soup until smooth, then reheat and season with salt and pepper.
soupe-de-legumes-au-b-uf: Brown the minced beef in the margarine over medium-high heat.
Add the onion and cook until soft.
Pour in the stock and water, add the celery and basil, bring to the boil, cover and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the tomato, carrot and pasta, bring back to the boil, then cook uncovered for 25 minutes.
Stir in the spinach, cook for a further 5 minutes, then serve.
soupe-de-poulet-au-riz-complet: Cut the chicken breast into small pieces.
Boil the chicken in the chicken stock for about 1 hour, stirring often.
Add the onion, celery, carrot, rice and seasoning, then leave to simmer for 1 to 1 hour 30 minutes, stirring regularly.
Add the parsley, then season with salt and pepper to taste before serving.
soupe-de-poulet-aux-macaronis: Fry the finely chopped onion and garlic in the butter without burning them.
Add the chicken, season with salt and pepper, and cook without browning.
Pour in the water, bring to the boil, skim off the foam, then cook the macaroni for 7 minutes.
Add the carrot and cabbage, adjust the seasoning, then stir in the evaporated milk off the heat without letting it boil.
Serve immediately, as the macaroni soaks up the broth quickly.
soupe-de-poulet-aux-pates: Rehydrate the mushrooms in hot water, then drain and squeeze them.
Flour the chicken pieces. Heat the butter and olive oil, then brown the chicken for 5 to 7 min and set aside.
Sauté the onion, garlic, thyme, basil and rosemary for 5 min over a medium heat until the onion turns golden.
Add the stock and water, bring to a gentle simmer, then add the chicken cut into pieces, the mushrooms, the peas and the carrots. Cook for 5 min.
Add the pasta and celery, cook for 5 min, then stir in the parsley and lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper, and serve.
soupe-de-poulet-aux-quenelles: Cook the quenelles for 7 min in simmering salted water, then set them aside on a board.
Melt the butter over a low heat, add the carrots, leek, onion, bay leaf and salt, then cook for 30 min with a lid on.
Pour in the stock, simmer for 30 min, then strain and discard the vegetables.
Thicken with the roux in several additions, simmer for 30 min, skimming as you go.
Add the quenelles, the chicken, the honey and thyme glazed carrots and celery, sprinkle with chives and serve piping hot.
soupe-de-poulet-a-la-creme-et-au-citron: Chicken soup with cream and lemon
Soften the finely sliced onion, celery and carrot in olive oil over medium-low heat with a pinch of salt, until the onion is translucent.
Add the chicken, stock, lemon juice and zest, thyme, rosemary and bay leaf, then bring to the boil.
Reduce the heat, cover and simmer for 30 minutes.
Remove the herbs, stir in the cream, season with salt and pepper, then serve with the green salad and cucumber.
soupe-de-riz-et-b-uf: Pour the rice, water, parsley, chives, rosemary and pepper into a rice cooker or a large saucepan.
Start cooking and cover until it simmers.
Add the minced beef and the cinnamon, cover again and cook for 60 min over a low heat.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve hot with the green salad and the tomatoes in salad.
soupe-de-tomates-aux-herbes: Fry the finely sliced onion in the olive oil until soft, without colouring.
Add the tomatoes, chicken stock, tomato sauce, basil, thyme and pepper.
Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat, cover and simmer for 20 min.
Off the heat, stir in the balsamic vinegar, then pour into bowls and garnish with fresh basil strips.
soupe-de-tripes-bulgare-shkembe-chorba: Melt the butter and fry the sliced onion and red pepper for 5 minutes.
Sprinkle in the flour, then stir in the tomato purée.
Add the tripe cut into thin strips, the beef stock, the salt, the marjoram and the bay leaf.
Cover partially and simmer for 30 minutes, then remove the bay leaf.
Mix the parsley, crushed garlic and grated cheese, sprinkle over the hot soup and serve straight away with vegetables on the side.
soupe-galicienne-aux-pois-chiches: Blend 430 g of drained chickpeas with the vegetable stock until smooth.
Heat the olive oil, sauté the onion for 5 min, then add the potato, carrot, celery and salt for 5 min.
Add the purée, the remaining chickpeas, the bay leaf, the mustard and the cumin, bring to the boil, then simmer covered for 30 min.
Stir in the peas, the vinegar and the tomato, season with pepper, add the cayenne pepper and cook for another 5 min.
Serve the soup sprinkled with finely chopped basil.
soupe-goulash: Cut the beef and potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes, finely slice the onion and warm the stock.
Brown the minced meat in the oil over medium-high heat, then drain on kitchen paper.
Fry the caraway seeds in the oil for 1 min, add the onion and cook gently until it turns golden.
Add the meat, vinegar, stock, potatoes and tomato purée, then stir in the sweet paprika.
Season with marjoram, thyme, hot paprika, bay leaf and pepper, then leave to simmer for 30 min.
soupe-libyenne-sharba: Fry the finely chopped onion and garlic in the olive oil for 3 minutes until translucent.
Add the diced lamb and brown on all sides, stirring.
Add the carrot, potato, celery, peppers, courgette, peas, chickpeas, tomato, tomato purée and spices, season with salt and pepper, then cover with water.
Bring to the boil, reduce the heat and simmer for 1 hour, then add the macaroni and cook for 10 minutes.
Serve piping hot, sprinkled with chopped parsley.
soupe-mbamba-gambienne: Soak the dried catfish for 30 minutes, remove the bones and flake the flesh.
Fry the onion and garlic in the palm oil until soft.
Add the tomato, tomato purée, ginger and paprika, then mix with the pumpkin, okra and aubergine.
Cover with water, simmer gently for 30 minutes, then add the fish for 10 minutes. Serve with brown rice.
soupe-rwandaise-aux-haricots-et-au-poiss: Fry the finely chopped onion and garlic in the oil for 3 minutes until translucent.
Add the tomato, carrot, potato, cooked beans, bay leaf, cumin and thyme, then cover with water.
Simmer for 25 minutes, then add the fish cut into pieces and continue for 5 minutes, salt and pepper.
Remove the bay leaf, adjust the seasoning and serve hot with chopped parsley.
soupe-toscane-sans-viande: Fry the sliced onion and carrot in olive oil until the onion is soft.
Add the chicken stock and water, season with salt and pepper, and bring to the boil.
Stir in the white beans and pasta, and bring back to the boil.
Reduce the heat, cover and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring from time to time, until the pasta and vegetables are tender.
Add the finely sliced endive and heat for 2 minutes before serving.
soupe-egyptienne-aux-lentilles: Heat the olive oil over a medium heat, then fry the chopped onion until it becomes translucent and lightly golden.
Add the chopped garlic and cook for 1 min, then stir in the lentils and spices (cumin, coriander, paprika, turmeric).
Pour in the vegetable stock, bring to the boil, then reduce the heat and cover to cook for 20 to 25 min until the lentils are tender.
Blend the soup until smooth and velvety, then return it to the pan and add the lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Reheat for a few minutes and serve hot, sprinkled with chopped parsley.
soupe-epicee-nigeriane-aux-ufs: Fry the onion and garlic in the vegetable oil over a medium heat until the onion turns translucent.
Add the pepper and tomato and cook for a few minutes until the vegetables soften.
Add the stock, cayenne pepper, paprika, cumin and coriander, season with salt, then bring to a simmer.
Pour the beaten eggs in a thin stream into the simmering soup, stirring gently to form fine strands, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes.
Adjust the seasoning, remove from the heat and serve hot with brown rice.
spaghetti-aux-palourdes: Bring 4 litres of salted water to the boil, then cook the spaghetti for 7 to 8 minutes until al dente.
Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large frying pan, add the garlic and the pepperoncini chilli, and fry for 1 minute without letting them burn.
Add the live clams and the chopped tomatoes, cover and cook for 8 minutes, shaking the pan, and discard any clams that remain closed.
Drain the pasta, add it to the pan with the clams, lower the heat, then stir in the tinned clams and the clam juice.
Season with salt, toss the pasta in the sauce, sprinkle with chopped parsley and serve hot.
spaghettis-au-poulet-et-au-poivre-noir: Spaghetti with chicken and black pepper
Cook the spaghetti for 10 min in boiling water with the oil, then drain, keeping a little of the cooking water.
Poach the chicken pieces in salted water until they change colour, then drain.
Fry the garlic, pepper and onion in the remaining oil in a non-stick pan.
Add the chicken, cream, black pepper, salt and parsley, then mix.
Add the spaghetti, toss together and serve hot.
spaghettis-aux-fruits-de-mer: Finely slice the onion, chop the garlic and zest the lemon, keeping the juice.
Soften the onion and lemon zest in the olive oil, add the seafood and cook for 5 min.
Add the garlic, tomato purée and lemon juice, moisten with the white wine, season and cook for 10 min.
Cook the spaghetti until al dente, tip it over the seafood, toss together and add the cream.
Leave to rest for 2 min, then serve.
steak-de-filet-de-b-uf-a-la-sauce-au-vin: Beef Fillet Steak with Red Wine Sauce
Mix the crushed black pepper, salt and finely chopped garlic, then rub the mixture over both sides of the steaks.
Grill the steaks for 5 minutes on each side on a spray-oiled ridged griddle until cooked to your liking, then keep warm.
Sweat the thinly sliced onion for 5 minutes with the lid on in a greased non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Deglaze the pan with the red wine, reduce for 1 minute, then stir in the steak sauce.
Spoon the red wine sauce over the steaks, top with the onion and serve.
steak-grille-aux-herbes: Let the beef thaw for about 1 hour if needed.
Preheat the grill over a moderate heat.
Season the meat with salt and herbs, then add the garlic powder and a light sprinkling of coriander.
Grill for 7 to 10 minutes per side, then allow a further 5 minutes for medium-done cooking.
Let rest for 3 minutes before serving with wholegrain rice and a tomato salad.
steak-pane-a-la-texane: Heat the bacon fat in a cast-iron pan over medium-high heat.
Beat the eggs with the paprika, salt and pepper, then dip the steaks in the mixture.
Coat each steak in flour on both sides, then brown them for 4 minutes per side in the hot pan.
Deglaze with the stock, add the milk and cream mixture and let the sauce thicken over low heat, then spoon it over the steaks and serve with potatoes and green beans.
superkanja-gambienne: Fry the sliced onion and garlic in the vegetable oil over a medium heat until soft.
Add the minced meat and brown it, stirring regularly.
Stir in the tomato, tomato purée, ginger, paprika, then the okra and aubergine.
Cover with water or stock, bring to the boil, then simmer covered for 30 min, until the vegetables are cooked.
Add the spinach, let it wilt for 5 min, adjust the seasoning and serve with brown rice.
supreme-de-poulet-au-miel-et-a-la-moutar: Chicken supreme with honey and mustard
Melt the butter in a frying pan, add the honey, mustard and curry powder, and stir to combine.
Add the chicken breast and coat it in the sauce.
Cook over a medium heat for 45 minutes, basting regularly and turning the chicken halfway through cooking.
Serve with wholegrain rice and a tomato salad.
suqaar-saute-de-b-uf-epice-a-la-somalien: Heat the vegetable oil over medium-high heat in a large frying pan, then soften the thinly sliced onion until tender.
Add the chopped garlic and minced beef, cooking and breaking it up until the meat is well browned.
Stir in the diced tomato and thinly sliced red pepper, sauté for 3 minutes, then sprinkle over the cumin, coriander, turmeric and cayenne pepper and mix well.
Season with salt, lower the heat, cover and simmer for a few minutes so the flavours can meld.
Scatter over chopped fresh coriander or parsley and serve with brown rice.
tafelspitz-b-uf-bouilli-aux-legumes: Bring a large casserole of salted water to the boil over a medium heat.
Add the meat, garlic, peppercorns and juniper berries, then cover.
Bring back to the boil, add the carrots, onion and parsley, cover and leave to simmer for 60 minutes.
Turn the meat over, season with salt, cover and continue cooking for 90 minutes.
Switch off the heat, leave the meat to rest in the stock for 20 minutes, then slice thinly against the grain and serve with the vegetables.
tagine-de-poulet-aux-carottes: Heat the olive oil in a casserole dish, then fry the finely chopped onion and garlic until soft.
Add the chicken and brown it lightly, then stir in the cumin, paprika, salt and pepper.
Add the chopped tomato and carrot, pour in 250 ml of water and cover.
Leave to simmer over a low heat for 35 min until the meat is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Serve piping hot with wholemeal bread and a tomato salad.
tajine-bil-samak-tajine-de-poisson-libye: Tajine bil samak, Libyan fish tajine
Heat the olive oil over a medium heat in the tajine, then fry the finely sliced onion and garlic until they become translucent.
Lightly brown the fish for 2 minutes on each side, then set aside.
Add the diced tomato and tomato paste, then stir in the cumin, paprika, cayenne pepper, coriander, caraway, salt, pepper and water.
Return the fish to the sauce, cover and leave to simmer for 10 to 15 minutes until it flakes easily with a fork.
Sprinkle with chopped parsley and serve hot with bread.
tajine-de-poulet-au-citron-et-aux-olives: Chicken tagine with lemon and olives
Marinate the chicken in the lemon juice for 30 minutes in the fridge, then pat dry with kitchen paper.
Mix the flour, salt, pepper, red chilli and turmeric, then coat the chicken.
Brown the chicken for 3 minutes on each side in the hot olive oil, then set aside.
Soften the onion, ginger and garlic, then add the chicken, stock, olives, lemon zest and cinnamon.
Bring to the boil, cover and simmer for 1 hour, then remove the cinnamon and scatter with coriander before serving with brown rice and a tomato salad.
taquitos-au-b-uf-hache-et-a-la-pomme-de-: Boil the potatoes for 30 minutes in simmering water, drain, then mash until smooth.
Boil the tomato, jalapeño, serrano pepper and half of the onion for 10 to 15 minutes, then blend with the garlic, a little salt and the coriander.
Brown the minced beef with the sliced onion, the chopped tomato, garlic salt, cumin and pepper until fully coloured.
Fry the tortillas for 15 to 20 seconds per side in hot oil, then drain on kitchen paper.
Fill each tortilla with mash and beef, roll them up, then serve warm with the tomato sauce.
tarte-au-saumon-et-aux-epinards: Preheat the oven to 220 °C and cook the spinach for 2 min in boiling water, then drain and roughly chop.
In a mixing bowl, whisk the eggs with the crème fraîche, the coriander, salt and pepper.
Line a tart tin with the puff pastry, spread over the salmon and spinach, then pour in the cream mixture.
Bake for 25 min at 220 °C and serve the tart warm with a salad of baby spinach leaves.
tchakpolo-ragout-togolais-de-viande-et-l: Tchakpolo, Togolese meat and vegetable stew
Fry the finely chopped onion and garlic in the vegetable oil until translucent.
Add the meat in pieces and brown on all sides, then stir in the tomato, pepper and sliced carrot.
Dilute the tomato purée with a little water, add the spices, ginger, salt and pepper, then pour in the stock.
Simmer gently for 1 hour to 1 hour 30 minutes until the meat is tender, then thicken with the diluted peanut butter.
Sprinkle with chopped parsley or coriander and serve hot with wholegrain rice.
tchari-riz-jollof: Fry the thinly sliced onion in the vegetable oil until it becomes translucent.
Add the garlic, ginger, tomato, peppers and blended chilli, then cook for 10 minutes, stirring, until thickened.
Stir in the thyme, curry, paprika, nutmeg and bay leaf, then the rinsed rice and the chicken.
Pour in the stock, season with salt and pepper, bring to the boil, then cover and simmer gently for 20 minutes.
Add the peas, leave to rest covered for a few minutes, then serve hot.
thon-a-la-catalane: Peel and deseed the tomatoes, then cut them into dice.
Oil a heavy-based casserole, pour in the tomatoes and place the tuna on top.
Season with salt, cayenne pepper and chopped coriander, cover and bring gently to the boil, then leave to simmer for 5 min.
Add the tomato coulis and the remaining oil, and continue cooking for 10 min.
Stir in the sliced gherkins and the confit onions, and serve cold with bread.
tofu-saltado: Mix 1 tbsp of soy sauce with 1 tsp of chilli oil, then marinate the tofu cut into cubes.
Cut the potatoes into 1 cm cubes, fry them for 15 to 20 minutes in the vegetable oil, then drain on kitchen paper.
Sauté the sliced onion for 5 minutes, add the pepper cut into large pieces and cook for 3 minutes.

Add the tomato in wedges, the garlic, the cumin, the coriander, the vinegar, the remaining soy sauce, the chilli oil and 5 tbsp of water, cook for 5 minutes, then return the tofu with the chopped coriander and mint.
Serve the tofu on top of the fried potatoes, sprinkled with fresh herbs.
tofu-tandoori: Cut the firm tofu into 2.5 cm cubes, then spread them on a tray and bake for 20 minutes at 200 °C to dry them out.
In a bowl, mix the turmeric, tomato sauce, Greek yoghurt, olive oil and hot sauce.
Marinate the tofu cubes in this mixture in the fridge for about 8 hours.
Thread the cubes onto skewers and grill until golden.
Serve with brown rice and a green salad.
tofu-a-la-sichuanaise: Fry the thinly sliced onion with the ginger and chillies for 3 minutes.
Add the minced meat and crushed garlic and leave to brown for 4 minutes.
Stir in the cubed tofu, miso, soy sauce, rice wine and ground Sichuan pepper.
Simmer for 8 minutes over a low heat, scatter with spring onion and serve with brown rice and a green salad.
tom-kha-kai-soupe-thai-au-poulet-et-au-l: Tom kha kai, Thai chicken and coconut soup
Bring the stock and coconut milk to the boil.
Add the lemongrass, galangal, chilli, sugar and pepper, then the onion, tomato, chicken and mushrooms.
Let it boil vigorously for 4 min, then remove from the heat.
Stir in the lime juice and soy sauce, garnish with coriander and serve with brown rice.
tomates-farcies-a-l-agneau: Mix the minced lamb, tomato passata, thinly sliced mushrooms, onion and crushed garlic, then season with salt and pepper.
Scoop out the tomatoes, fill them with the mixture, then replace their tops.
Arrange the tomatoes in an ovenproof dish with a drizzle of olive oil and half a glass of water.
Bake for 40 min at 180 °C, then serve with wholewheat rice.
torti-aux-crevettes-et-a-la-feta: Cook the pasta until al dente in boiling salted water, then drain.
Peel the prawns and finely slice the onion.
Melt the butter over a low heat, brown the prawns over a medium heat, then add the onion and cook for 1 minute.
Add the diced feta and the crème fraîche, season with salt and pepper.
Toss with the pasta, sprinkle with finely chopped chives and serve with a green salad.
tourteline-a-la-truite-et-aux-poireaux: Bake the puff pastry base blind.
Thinly slice the leek and sweat it in butter with salt and pepper.
Poach the trout in a court-bouillon, then remove the skin and bones and flake it into small pieces.
Arrange the leek and trout on the base, pour over the milk beaten with the eggs, seasoned with salt and pepper, and bake for 15 to 20 minutes.
travers-de-porc-a-la-mijoteuse: Season the pork ribs generously with the rib rub, then refrigerate overnight.
Mix together the cider vinegar, honey, Worcestershire sauce, liquid smoke and flour.
Place the ribs at the bottom of the slow cooker, pour the mixture over the top, cover and cook on low for 8 to 9 hours.
Serve hot with a green salad and carrots.
tripes-a-la-mode-de-caen: Tripes à la mode de Caen
Place an upturned plate in the bottom of the tripière, cut the tripe into 4 to 5 cm squares and arrange the carrots, onion, leek and the muslin bag of herbs on top.
Season with salt, add the tripe, then pour in cider and calvados to just cover the meat.
Seal the lid with a paste of flour and water, then cook for 15 hours at 100 °C without ever letting it boil.
Skim the fat from the broth, remove the bag of herbs and serve piping hot, moistened with cider.
truite-aux-amandes: Preheat the oven to 200 °C and place the trout in a dish.
Cover the trout with almonds, pour over the white wine, season with salt and pepper, and add the fresh herbs.
Melt the butter in a frying pan, brown the remaining almonds, then deglaze with the cooking juices and let it simmer for a few bubbles.
Serve the trout topped with the almond sauce, with brown rice and green salad.
veau-aux-haricots-de-lima: Rinse the meat under cold water, drain, then brown it with the butter and onion over medium-high heat for a few minutes.
Season with salt, pepper and water, add 2 to 3 tablespoons of tomatoes, cover and bring to the boil.
Trim the lima beans, cut them in half if desired, then add them to the meat after a few minutes of boiling, with enough water to cover everything.
Add the remaining tomatoes once the beans are cooked, then simmer for a few minutes to thicken the juices.
vindaloo-de-poulet: Caramelise the thinly sliced onions in oil over low, then medium heat, add the vinegar and let it reduce, then blend with a little oil into a brown sauce.
Blend the garlic, chilli and ginger, then add the turmeric, ground coriander, garam masala and cinnamon.
Brown the cut chicken in the hot oil with the spice paste until golden.
Add the onion sauce and a little water, then cook covered for 30 to 40 minutes over low heat, stirring occasionally.
Serve the vindaloo on basmati rice and sprinkle with fresh coriander.
vorschmack-boulettes-finlandaises: Soak the herring fillets in cold water overnight, then pat them dry on kitchen paper.
Preheat the oven to 220 °C, then brown the lamb, beef and onion for 15 to 20 minutes in a greased dish.
Blend the meat, onion, herring and anchovies, then add water, garlic and white pepper until you reach a thick porridge-like texture.
Spread the tomato purée over the mixture and bake for 2 hours at 175 °C, adding water if needed.
waakyne-riz-et-haricots-a-il-noir-ghanee: Waakye, Ghanaian rice and black-eyed beans
Sort the black-eyed beans, rinse them, then drain and place them in a pressure cooker.
Add the dried millet leaves and enough water to cover the beans by a few centimetres, then close the pressure cooker.
Cook under pressure for 15 minutes, then leave on a low heat for a further 15 minutes, and allow to cool naturally for about 20 minutes.
Transfer the contents to another saucepan, add the rice and a little water if needed, season with salt, then simmer on a low heat until fully cooked.
Remove the millet leaves and serve with a green salad and tomato salad.
yassa-poulet-gambien: Mix the onions, garlic, ginger, lemon juice, olive oil, mustard, pepper and a pinch of salt, then add the chicken and leave to marinate in the fridge for at least 2 hours.
Heat the vegetable oil over medium-high heat and brown the drained chicken for 5 to 7 minutes on each side.
Add the reserved marinade, cover and simmer over medium heat for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring from time to time.
Sprinkle with chopped parsley and serve with brown rice.
yassa-poulet-senegalais: Rinse the chicken, pat it dry, then marinate it for 2 to 12 hours with the garlic, onions, mustard, lemon juice, salt, stock, cayenne pepper and paprika.
Drain the chicken and set the marinade aside with the onions.
Brown the chicken for 5 minutes on each side in the hot olive oil, then set aside.
Fry the onions with the marinade for 5 minutes over a medium heat, return the chicken, pour in the stock and leave to simmer for 20 minutes until fully cooked, then adjust the seasoning.
Serve the chicken and its juices with brown rice.
zupa-ogorkowa-soupe-polonaise-au-concomb: Bring 1.5 L of cold water to the boil with the chicken wings, bay leaf, sweet paprika, salt and pepper, then leave to simmer over a low heat for 25 min.
Add the peeled carrot, parsnip and leek, and cook for a further 10 min.
Remove the leek, add the potatoes cut into 6 mm dice and cook for 10 to 12 min until tender.
Grate the cucumbers and fry them for 2 min in the melted butter, then add the flour and stir over a low heat.
Dilute with 80 to 120 ml of water, pour into the pan, cook for 3 to 5 min, adjust the seasoning and serve.
c-lb-r-ufs-poches-au-yaourt: Mix the Greek yoghurt with the crushed garlic clove and a pinch of salt.
Poach the eggs for 3 minutes in simmering water with vinegar and salt added.
Lift the eggs out with a slotted spoon and arrange them on two plates.
Spoon the garlic yoghurt over the eggs, then melt the butter and stir in the paprika.
Pour the warm paprika butter over the eggs and serve straight away with wholemeal bread and a tomato salad.
uf-bocage: Boil the potatoes in water, then mash them.
Add the butter, the cheese, the chopped parsley, salt and pepper, then mix well.
Spread the mixture in a gratin dish, make hollows and crack the eggs into them.
Sprinkle with Gruyère and bake for 8 to 10 minutes, then serve with a tomato salad.
